title: 第7章　伊斯坦布尔的门槛：异化与边缘经验
originalTitle: CHAPTER 7 Istanbul’s Threshold: Alienation and the Experience of the Periphery

zh: 第7章　伊斯坦布尔的门槛：异化与边缘经验
en: CHAPTER 7 Istanbul’s Threshold: Alienation and the Experience of the Periphery

zh: 艾汉·盖奇金的《在边缘》（2003）与哈蒂杰·梅里耶姆的《人各有别》（2008），是两部差别相当大的小说：《在边缘》严肃而阴郁，《人各有别》则幽默而轻快。然而，两者都以边缘概念为核心，既将其作为主题，也将其作为故事场景。因此，异化与隔绝的问题是两部作品的中心。尽管它们在情节、风格及其他形式特征上有所不同，这一相似之处仍提供了富于启发性的比较基础；两本书都以生活在伊斯坦布尔昔日棚户区的第一代和／或第二代迁入者的生活为题材。
en: (2003) by Ayhan Geçgin and
(2008) by Hatice Meryem are two novels considerably different from each other:
is a sober and rather grim novel;

is a highly humorous and light-hearted one. However, both have the concept of the periphery at their centre, as a theme and as a setting. Therefore, issues of alienation and isolation are central to both works. This similarity, despite their differences in terms of plot as well as style and other formal characteristics, serves as an inspiring ground of comparison as the two books take the life of first and/or second-generation migrants living in former shanty towns of Istanbul as their subject matter.

zh: 《在边缘》：阴郁城市中的存在
en: On the Periphery: Existence in the Grim City

zh: 艾汉·盖奇金2003年出版的处女作《在边缘》（Kenarda），在阴郁的氛围中讲述主人公的记忆，以及他的家人和大家族成员迁往伊斯坦布尔、在这座城市中奋斗的故事。书名既暗示贫困街区（
），也指作为城市边缘或郊区的外围（
）。它还在存在意义上暗示，身处生活的边缘。在小说中，盖奇金既从物质必需品方面，也从迁入者在城市环境中需要社会与文化发展机会的方面，讨论城市权利。他将异化和隔绝主题与这些机会的缺失联系起来，并用阴郁意象强化它们。
en: In Ayhan Geçgin’s debut novel

), published in 2003, the protagonist’s memories as well as his family’s and extended family’s stories of migration to Istanbul and their struggle in this city are told through a grim atmosphere. Its title implies poor neighbourhoods (
) as well as the periphery (

) as the edge or outskirts of the city. The title also indicates being on the periphery of life existentially. In his novel, Geçgin addresses the right to the city both in terms of material necessities and the need for opportunities for migrants’ social and cultural development in the urban setting. He treats the themes of alienation and isolation in connection with the lack of such opportunities, reinforcing them by grim imagery.

zh: 这部没有明确情节的小说，以20世纪90年代末为背景，但更早的几十年也通过倒叙出现。开头几页描绘了主人公乘坐的锡尔凯吉—哈尔卡勒铁路线上的车站。这条线路于1955年启用，也被称为伊斯坦布尔通勤铁路。

列车停靠城市萨拉伊布尔努海岸沿线的詹库尔塔兰、库姆卡帕、耶尼卡帕街区，继续驶向包括历史城墙的科贾穆斯塔法帕夏与耶迪库莱，再停靠卡兹勒切什梅、泽伊廷布尔努、耶尼马哈莱和巴克尔柯伊；随后继续开往哈尔卡勒，在终点之前还停靠七站。全书多次出现这条铁路在卡兹勒切什梅—巴克尔柯伊一带的车站，都带着沉郁的色调，第一次出现时就是如此：“列车沿海岸从哈尔卡勒到锡尔凯吉往返行驶，从早到晚连接着无数几乎一模一样的街区。年复一年［……］，城市不断扩张，贫穷离开这里，又在那里加剧，棚屋［……］让位于几层或许多层的楼房”（Geçgin 2003，12）。叙述者补充说：“苦难［……］从一个街区奔向另一个街区”（12）。
en: The novel, which lacks an explicit plot, is set in the late 1990s, yet earlier decades also appear through flashbacks. The first pages include the depictions of the train station on the Sirkeci–Halkalı railway line, which the protagonist uses. Inaugurated in 1955, this line was also called the Istanbul commuter railway.

The train stopped at the neighbourhoods of Cankurtaran, Kumkapı and Yenikapı on the Sarayburnu shore of the city, continuing to Kocamustafapaşa and Yedikule, which included the historic city walls, then at Kazlıçeşme, Zeytinburnu, Yenimahalle and Bakırköy, before continuing to Halkalı, stopping at seven more stations before terminating there. Throughout the book, the railway line’s stations in the Kazlıçeşme–Bakırköy area appear at various instances, depicted in a depressing timbre, as is the case in the first instance: “the train was running forward and backward by the coast from Halkalı to Sirkeci connecting numerous, almost identical quarters from the morning until the night. As the years passed by [...] the city was expanding, poverty was leaving here and intensifying there, shanties were [...] leaving their places to buildings with a few or many storeys” (Geçgin 2003, 12). The narrator adds: “misery was running [...] from one neighbourhood to the other” (12).

zh: 第一章描写主人公居住的街区，并呈现关于城市的印象，介绍了作品的全部主要主题与形式特征：长而复杂的句子细致描绘环境，视觉与嗅觉意象强化了阴郁的氛围。本章提及主人公的家人与亲戚，强调他们是乡村迁入者。
en: Depictions of the neighbourhood where the protagonist lives as well as impressions about the city appear in this first chapter, introducing all the main themes, as well as formal characteristics of the work: long and complex sentences giving detailed descriptions of the setting and a grim atmosphere reinforced by visual and olfactory imagery. There are references to the protagonist’s family members and relatives in this chapter which stress that they are rural migrants.

zh: 盖奇金没有透露太多关于主人公的信息。通过“鬼魂”（Hortlak）的问题，我们推断他是男性。
关于他的外貌、教育或职业，都没有信息。有关他父系与母系亲属，以及相关村庄或街区中其他人物的段落，贯穿全书。人物就是这样进入作品的：他们并不是在情节线中行动的角色，而是出现在经由记忆浮现的各个独立故事中。
en: Geçgin does not disclose much information about the protagonist. Through Hortlak’s (Ghost’s) question we infer that he is male.

There is no information regarding his physical appearance, education or occupation. Passages about the members of his family and relatives, both on his mother’s and father’s side, as well as various other figures from related villages or neighbourhoods, appear throughout the book. This is the way characters enter the work, not as figures acting in a plot line but within separate stories that surface through memories.

zh: 小说没有交代主人公父母出身村庄的位置。这个村庄靠近几次被提到的达哲克镇（Dağcık）（78，119）；然而，它似乎是虚构的，因为土耳其市镇的官方数据库没有这个镇的记录（Belediyeler）。几处细节暗示，他们具有库尔德与阿列维派背景。在讲述祖父及近亲、远亲如何迁往伊斯坦布尔的段落中，叙述者解释说：“村庄要么渐渐空了，要么被疏空了”（35）。在土耳其现代史中，村庄人口流失主要发生在库尔德村庄，这是库尔德工人党与土耳其军队之间低烈度战争的结果。此外，“鬼魂”的问题中还有库尔德语词
。这里不妨指出，艾汉·盖奇金虽然母语是库尔德语，却是一位用土耳其语写作的作家（Üstündağ 2019，i）。
en: In the novel, there is no information regarding the location of the village where the protagonist’s parents come from. This village is near the town of Dağcık, which is mentioned a couple of times (78, 119); however, this seems to be a fictitious place, since there is no record of such a town in the official town database of Turkish municipalities (Belediyeler). A couple of details imply that they come from a Kurdish and Alevi background. In the passage about how Grandfather and his close and distant family migrated to Istanbul, the narrator explains: “villages either got empty gradually or they have been evacuated” (35). In the modern history of Turkey, depopulation of villages is chiefly something that has happened to Kurdish villages due to the low-intensity war between the PKK and the Turkish army. Added to that is the Kurdish word “
” in Ghost’s question. Here, it might be useful to note that Ayhan Geçgin is an author writing in Turkish although his mother tongue is Kurdish (Üstündağ 2019, i).

zh: 主人公、舅舅赛伊德，以及主人公外祖母的一位亲戚哈桑，一同去探望主人公姨母的丈夫比纳利；盖奇金借哈桑在谈话中使用的一种表达，揭示了他们的阿列维派身份。哈桑讲到自己的一次经历时，用下面这些话表达震惊：“我大吃一惊［……］，我说‘呀，穆罕默德，呀，阿里’，开始往回走”（91）。“Ya Muhammed ya Ali”是阿列维派在震惊或恐惧时表达信仰的说法。使用这一表达，暗示哈桑是阿列维派。哈桑与主人公母亲的家庭有亲属关系，因此，如果他是阿列维派，她也应是阿列维派。由于阿列维派，尤其乡村的阿列维派，通常与阿列维派通婚，这又意味着主人公的父亲及其家族也是阿列维派。
en: Geçgin reveals the Alevi identity in an expression Hasan, a relative of the protagonist’s grandmother, uses in a conversation when the protagonist, his mother’s brother Seyid, and Hasan go to visit Binali, the husband of the protagonist’s aunt. Talking about an experience he has had, Hasan expresses his shock in the following words: “I was very surprised [...], I said ‘ya Muhammed ya Ali’, started walking back” (91). “Ya Muhammed ya Ali” is an expression Alevis use to express faith when in a state of shock or fear. The use of the expression implies that Hasan is an Alevi. Since Hasan is related to the protagonist’s mother’s family, if he is an Alevi then she would also be an Alevi. As Alevis, especially rural ones, generally marry Alevis, this would mean that the protagonist’s father and his family are also Alevis.

zh: 全书讲述的迁移故事极为相似。第一个是祖父的故事，出现在第一章最后一节。他迁往伊斯坦布尔时，把两个儿子留在村里照管土地，由一个姐姐照顾他们。在伊斯坦布尔，祖父白天在工厂工作，夜里看守一座客商旅店，住在里面一间狭小、阴暗的屋子里。他的长子，也就是主人公的父亲，结婚后独自迁往伊斯坦布尔，没有带上妻子，开始与父亲同住。祖父身体不好，被迫离开工厂；过了一阵，他与儿子凑起积蓄，开始经营旅店里的茶铺。他租下一间带花园的棚屋后，怀孕的儿媳也来到这里。与此同时，祖父结了婚。他的小儿子离开村庄，加入他们。祖父的弟弟和年长的侄子也迁来伊斯坦布尔。这个过程被描述为：“不只是他们，他们的妻子、儿子、女儿、儿媳、女婿也来了”（35）。他们的近亲、远亲随后也迁往伊斯坦布尔：“有些人在这里安家，有些人在别的地区安家。在那些地区，他们住在特定街区，房子彼此挨近。有些人住在其他大城市，在那里繁衍。村里只剩非常年老的人；他们一死，那里就再也没人了。城镇和城市变得更大，也更加拥挤”（35）。这段用几句话概括乡城迁移现象，其机械式的风格值得注意。
en: The migration stories we hear throughout the book are remarkably similar. The first one of these is Grandfather’s story, which appears in the final section of the first chapter. As he migrates to Istanbul, he leaves his two sons in the village in charge of his land. One of his older sisters would be responsible for taking care of his sons. In Istanbul, Grandfather works in factories in the daytime and as the watchman of an inn at night, where he has a tiny, dark room to stay in. His older son, the protagonist’s father, gets married and migrates to Istanbul, without his wife, where he starts staying in his father’s room. Grandfather’s ill health forces him to leave his job at the factory and, after a while, he starts running the tea shop at the inn, combining his savings with his son’s. When he rents a shanty with a garden, his son’s pregnant wife joins them. In the meanwhile, Grandfather gets married. His younger son leaves the village and joins them. Grandfather’s younger brother and his older nephew also move to Istanbul. The process is explained as follows: “not only they but their wives, sons, daughters, daughters-in-law, sons-in-law also came” (35). Their close and distant relatives also move to Istanbul in due course: “Some of them moved in here some of them in other quarters. In those quarters, they lived in specific neighbourhoods in houses close to each other. Some lived in other big cities, multiplied there. In villages, very old people stayed, and once they died nobody was left there. Towns and cities became bigger and overcrowded” (35). The mechanical style in this passage, summarising the rural–urban migration phenomenon in a couple of sentences is worthy of note.

zh: 第一部的第三章讲述主人公母亲一家的迁移故事，重点在母亲的兄弟伊斯身上。父亲去世后，伊斯把村里的房地契留给三个妹妹和一个弟弟，来到伊斯坦布尔。这个过程被描述得简单而顺畅：“他从村子走了出来，来到这里”（62）。最终，他的弟妹和母亲都迁往伊斯坦布尔，在“城市边缘地区租下一栋半完工的房子”（62）。他的妹妹们开始在纺织作坊工作，弟弟则进了工厂。
en: The third chapter of the first book presents the migration story of the protagonist’s mother’s family with a focus on İs, his mother’s brother. After his father’s death, İs leaves the deeds at the village to his three sisters and one brother, all of whom are younger than him, and comes to Istanbul, which is described as a simple and smooth process: “he walked off from the village and came here” (62). Eventually, all his siblings, together with their mother migrate to Istanbul and rent “a semi-complete house in an area at the periphery of the city” (62). His sisters start working in textile workshops and his brother in a factory.

zh: 主人公母亲的姐妹之一居利斯坦，嫁给了叔伯之子比纳利。居利斯坦怀着第二个女儿时，比纳利决定追随已经迁往伊斯坦布尔的兄弟。于是，比纳利带着妻子和女儿来到城市，在家人的棚屋里住了一阵。这期间，比纳利先在祖父的茶铺工作，后来在一家皮革作坊找到工作，一家人租下了棚屋。他们的四个女儿开始在纺织作坊干活，只有一个被允许读书。另一个迁移故事属于祖父的弟弟侯赛因叔公。他比祖父晚四五年来到伊斯坦布尔，开始住在哈尔卡勒附近。他在当地一家白色家电工厂找到工人工作，一直干到退休。他们兄弟的儿子也带着妻子来到这里，凭侯赛因的介绍进入同一家工厂，也在那里工作到退休。
en: Gülistan, one of the sisters of the protagonist’s mother, is married to Binali, who is her uncle’s son. When Gülistan is pregnant with their second daughter, Binali decides to follow his brother, who has migrated to Istanbul. So Binali, his wife and daughter come to the city and stay with Binali’s family in their shanty for a while. During this time, Binali works in Grandfather’s tea house and then finds a job in a leather workshop, and the family rent a shanty. Their four daughters start working in textile workshops and only one of them is allowed to study. Another story of migration belongs to Grandfather’s younger brother, Uncle Hüseyin. He comes to Istanbul four or five years after Grandfather and starts living near Halkalı. He gets a job as a worker in the white goods factory there, where he works until his retirement. Their brother’s son as well comes with his wife and is employed at the same factory thanks to Hüseyin providing a reference. He also retires there.

zh: 这些讲述主人公家人与亲属迁移故事的段落，具有值得注意的现实主义特征。这些故事切合实际，触及迁移现象的核心方面，如亲属关系在迁移中的重要性、同乡之间的链式迁移、女性在迁移过程中的位置，以及棚户住房；读来仿佛是关于伊斯坦布尔乡村迁入者的社会学研究中的个案。下面这段关于在祖父茶铺工作的两名亲戚的叙述，就是很好的例子。这些年轻人初来时，先住在亲戚家，工作、存钱，然后结婚，搬进自己的家。叙述者以现实主义方式强调，他们余下的故事取决于能够在多大程度上融入城市经济：“有些人一辈子当工人，有些人一时有工作、一时失业；有些敢闯的人干一阵后会去经商，做起买卖，要是站稳了脚跟，就也成了老板，亲戚会来给他干活”（31）。
en: The realism in these passages on the migration stories of the protagonist’s family and relatives is noteworthy. With their compatibility with actualities, these stories addressing the central aspects of the migration phenomenon—such as the significance of kinship relations in migration, chain migration from the same home town, women’s position in the migration process, and shanty housing—sound like case studies in a piece of sociological research on rural migration to Istanbul. The following excerpt about Grandfather’s two relatives who work in his tea house is a good example. When these young men first arrive, they stay with a relative; they work and save money, then get married, and move to their own home. The narrator realistically stresses that the rest of their story depends on how much they can integrate into the urban economy: “some of them would spend all their lives as workers, some would sometimes be a worker sometimes unemployed, some go-getter might go into trade after working for a while, start a business, and if he lands on his feet he would also be an employer whose relatives would come and work for him” (31).

zh: 这些段落对城市中工人阶级迁入者生活的运行方式所作的洞察，也引人注意。有一处，叙述者把迁入者描绘为“一辈子都在劳动，把劳动当作美德，把全部价值观都建立在这上面”的人（60）。在这些解释中，叙述声音的语调是中性的，并不特别赞颂苦干。这里暗示，在20世纪70年代，经济地位向上流动是可能的，因为那时迁入者能得到的稳定工作比后来的几十年多：侯赛因和他的兄弟都在同一家白色家电工厂工作一生，并在那里退休。书中还提到棚户特赦使屋主获准拆掉棚屋、建起公寓，从而提高了他们的生活水平。
en: The insight into the dynamics of working-class migrant life in the city also attracts attention in these passages. In one example, the narrator describes migrants as people who “have worked all through their lives, adopted work as a virtue, built all their values on this” (60). The tone of the narrative voice is neutral in these explanations, it does not particularly bless hard work. Here, there is the implication that upward economic mobility was possible during the 1970s, when the number of steady jobs for migrants was higher than the following decades: both Hüseyin and his brother work in the same white goods factory all through their lives and retire from there. There is also a reference to the increase in shanty owners’ living standards as a result of the shanty amnesty, allowing them to build apartments replacing their shanties.
body.review: 此处原文为“both Hüseyin and his brother”；前文相关迁移故事（原166页）写的是侯赛因及其兄弟的儿子。两处亲属关系表述按底本分别保留。

zh: 盖奇金没有把迁入者的社会与文化发展作为问题展开。他笔下主人公家人的社会网络，主要由亲戚构成。关于比纳利那个读大学的女儿，信息不足。侯赛因的儿子成了工程师，却是个几乎不出房间、不与人交往的人。主人公也在读书，但不清楚处于哪个教育阶段（34）。有关伊斯社会生活的信息，则相对详细，下文将加以讨论。
en: Geçgin does not problematise the social and cultural development of migrants. He portrays the protagonist’s family members as having a social network mainly comprising their relatives. There is not sufficient information about Binali’s daughter who is a university student. Hüseyin’s son, who becomes an engineer, turns out to be an anti-social figure who almost never leaves his room. The protagonist also studies, yet it is unclear at which level (34). Information on İs’s social life is rather detailed, as discussed below.

zh: 在《在边缘》中，男性故事多于女性故事。一些男人，如主人公的父亲、伊斯和“达伊奇人”（Dağiçili，来自达伊奇的人），曾沉迷于饮酒与夜生活。然而，来到城市的男人大多数都努力工作、节俭储蓄。在居利斯坦与比纳利、侯赛因及其家人的迁移故事中，女孩教育的主题短暂进入小说。比纳利让女儿们上小学，只因为这是义务教育（82）。他允许其中一个继续读书，另外三个则在纺织作坊工作。同样，侯赛因也不送女儿们上学。盖奇金在小说中暗示，女性的生活在迁移后并没有多大改变。作为重要母题出现的纺织作坊，似乎对应着乡村的田地：村里的女人整天在田间劳动，傍晚回家做所有家务、照顾孩子、做饭；换言之，在城里，作坊取代了田地。“几百个年轻女孩在其中工作的地下室纺织作坊”（18），简短而有力地描绘了工人阶级女性的环境。这些描写中，叙述声音冷淡的语调引人注意。小说中，盖奇金没有表现出对女性成为工人阶级成员时的心态的任何关注，也没有提及那些被丈夫禁止外出工作的迁入女性。他同样没有讨论女性因迁移而发生的观念变化。
en: In

, stories of men prevail over women. Some of the men, such as the protagonist’s father, İs, and Dağiçili (the one from Dağiçi) have been involved with alcohol and nightlife. However, the majority of men who came to the city have worked hard and saved money. Within the context of the migration stories of Gülistan and Binali, and Hüseyin and his family, the theme of girls’ education briefly enters the novel. Binali sends his daughters to primary school simply because it is compulsory (82). He allows one of them to study further, while the other three girls work in textile workshops. Similarly, Hüseyin does not send his daughters to school. Geçgin implies in his novel that not much changes in women’s lives upon migration. Textile workshops, which come to the fore as an important motif, seem like the counterpart of fields in the rural areas of the country: women living in villages work in the fields all day and in the evening they come home and do all the housework, childcare and cooking; in other words, in the city, workshops replace the fields. “Textile workshops in the basements where hundreds of young girls work” (18) is a simple yet powerful description of the working-class women’s environment. The indifferent tone of the narrative voice in such descriptions attracts attention. In the novel, Geçgin does not hint at any sort of awareness of women’s mentality as they become members of the working class, and makes no mention of migrant women who are not allowed to work by their husbands. Neither does he address the changes in perspectives of women due to migration.

zh: 另一个伊斯坦布尔

小说的主要场景，是主人公与家人居住的因吉尔柯伊街区、他的家人曾经工作的塔什勒巴街区，以及较为发达、因而成为邻近街区社会文化生活中心的巴克尔库莱。塔什勒巴再现的是泽伊廷布尔努区的卡兹勒切什梅街区。在20世纪90年代各工厂迁往伊斯坦布尔周边的科贾埃利与乔尔卢以前，它一直是皮革工业中心。“陵墓”（129）指阿里老爹陵墓，而带有鹅图案的“废弃喷泉”（130），指的是赋予这一区域名称的卡兹勒切什梅，即“鹅喷泉”。
en: The primary setting of the novel is the neighbourhoods of İncirköy, where the protagonist and his family live, that of Taşlıbağ where members of his family used to work, and that of Bakırkule which is a more developed area and therefore the centre of social and cultural life for the adjacent neighbourhoods. Taşlıbağ is a representation of the Kazlıçeşme neighbourhood of Zeytinburnu district. It was a centre for the leather industry until the 1990s when the factories were moved to cities in the Istanbul region: Kocaeli and Çorlu. “The tomb” (129) refers to the Ali Baba Tomb and the “defunct fountain” with figures of a goose (130) refers to the Kazlıçeşme (The Fountain with a Goose) which gives the area its name.

zh: 因吉尔柯伊是“沿海岸像牙齿一样排开、处于一个并不存在的中心边缘的街区之一”（12），似乎再现了卡兹勒切什梅的住宅部分。虚构的因吉尔柯伊是一个典型的旧棚户区，正在经历转变：棚屋被拆除，原地建起底层开设商铺的公寓楼。叙述者解释说，“街区以绵延多年的缓慢速度，呈现出适合当今世界的模样”，随后继续描写其他使这里显得“几乎‘现代’”的发展（12）。
en: İncirköy, “one of the neighbourhoods lined up like teeth along the coast at the periphery of a non-existent centre” (12), seems to be a representation of the residential parts of Kazlıçeşme. Fictional İncirköy is a typical former shanty town which undergoes a transformation as shanties are demolished and apartments are built on their site with shops on their ground floor. The narrator explains that “the neighbourhood took on an appearance that fits today’s world, with a slowness that spread out through the years” and continues by describing other developments in the place which made it look “almost ‘modern’” (12).

zh: 小说中的巴克尔库莱似乎是巴克尔柯伊的虚构对应地，火车站与林荫大道暗示了这一点。

居兹科南是另一个位于城市边缘的棚户区，主人公的一些家人住在那里。它可能受到加齐奥斯曼帕夏区某个街区的启发，线索如下：伊斯与主人公从托普卡帕乘小巴去居兹科南；那里有一条溪流，“污水在里面流淌，散发令人难以忍受的臭味”（79）。叙述者描述当地的房屋，说它们“以不完整、半完工的外观，成为街区的典型建筑”（72）。然而，关于居兹科南现实对应地的这些线索，并不像因吉尔柯伊、塔什勒巴与巴克尔库莱的线索那样有力。
en: In the novel, Bakırkule seems to be the fictional counterpart of Bakırköy, as the train station and the boulevard imply.

Güzkonan, another shanty town on the periphery of the city, where some members of the protagonist’s family live, might be inspired by one of the neighbourhoods of the Gaziosmanpaşa district, because of the following clues: İs and the protagonist go to Güzkonan using minibuses from Topkapı, and the place has a stream “where sewage waters flow with intolerable smells” (79). The narrator describes the houses in the area by saying they “have become the typical architecture of the neighbourhood with their incompleteness, half-finished appearance” (72). However, these clues about the factual counterpart of Güzkonan are not as strong as those for İncirköy, Taşlıbağ and Bakırkule.

zh: 除上述场景外，书中还有伊斯坦布尔两个虚构地区。其中一个是托兹卡帕，再现锡尔凯吉—哈尔卡勒铁路沿线的一个街区。涉及托兹卡帕时，一个真实街区与一个虚构街区出现在同一句话里：“在库姆卡帕和托兹卡帕，挤作一团的工人会不耐烦地等着火车”（25）。作品中另一处虚构地区叫迪兹格尔，被描述为靠近真实的哈尔卡勒地区（118）。
en: In addition to the above-mentioned settings, there are two more fictitious areas of Istanbul in the book. One of these is Tozkapı, which represents a neighbourhood on the Sirkeci–Halkalı railway. In the case of Tozkapı, within the same sentence a factual neighbourhood and a fictitious one appear together: “in Kumkapı and Tozkapı, a tightly packed group of workers would be waiting for the train impatiently” (25). The other fictitious area in the work is a place called Düzgöl, described as near the factual area of Halkalı (118).

zh: 于是问题来了：为什么小说中有些街区被掩去了真名？盖奇金将它们纳入书中，又加以伪装，或许是在暗示边缘街区既在城市之内、又在城市之外的矛盾位置。然而，书中以虚构名称出现的卡兹勒切什梅、巴克尔柯伊与加齐奥斯曼帕夏各有特征，很难归为一类。此外，巴克尔柯伊区的多个街区属于社会经济地位优越的居民，巴克尔柯伊广场也是重要的社会文化中心。总而言之，书中没有足够证据回答这个问题。
en: So, the question arises: why are some neighbourhoods disguised in the novel? As Geçgin includes them in the book but also disguises them, he may be implying the ambivalent position of the periphery neighbourhoods as being both in and out of the city. However, the areas of Kazlıçeşme, Bakırköy and Gaziosmanpaşa which appear under fictitious names in the book, have their own characteristics and are difficult to categorise together. Moreover, various neighbourhoods of the Bakırköy district belong to socioeconomically privileged inhabitants, and Bakırköy Square is an important social and cultural hub. In conclusion, there is not sufficient evidence in the book to answer the question.

zh: 博斯普鲁斯海峡、金角湾、众多其他景观，以及迷人的历史遗产，使人们普遍认为伊斯坦布尔是一座美得令人惊叹的城市。盖奇金反驳这一看法。要做到这一点，只需把目光投向城中大量不堪入目的区域，并不困难。然而，盖奇金在小说中并不局限于描写昔日棚户区或郊外工业区的丑陋；他在城市最受赞赏的部分也找到了阴暗。例如，主人公坐在卡拉柯伊，凝望几乎让所有人着迷的加拉塔景观，眼前所见却被描述为：“僵局一直蔓延到视线尽头”（152—153）。同样，当叙述者讲述他坐在长椅上望向托普卡帕宫时，历史遗产的光晕完全缺席（156）。雄伟的加拉塔塔被描绘为“带着干瘪的骄傲耸立［……］，其黑暗时隐时现”（160）。历史遗产与遗物多次作为把城市描绘成鬼城的意象进入作品：“一座破败的宏伟建筑和一座五百年历史的老建筑，使荒凉感更加强烈”（20）；一座“带穹顶的废弃大理石喷泉，尽管体量庞大，却不值得注意”（192）；“远处破败的防御工事，墙壁开裂，塔楼磨蚀或毁坏，像生锈的锯子向海岸延伸”（67）；“灰泥与装饰剥落的加拉塔老建筑”（98）。
en: With the Bosporus, the Golden Horn and numerous other sights, as well as its fascinating historical heritage, the general opinion is that Istanbul is a stunningly beautiful city. Geçgin refutes this claim. Doing this by spotlighting the unsightly areas of the city, which are abundant, would not be difficult. However, in his novel Geçgin does not confine himself to depicting the ugliness of former shanty towns or industrial areas on the outskirts; he finds bleakness in the city’s most admired parts. For instance, as the protagonist sits in Karaköy and stares at Galata, a sight that is fascinating for almost everybody, what he sees is described as follows: “deadlock was expanding as far as the eye can see” (152–153). Similarly, the aura of historical heritage is entirely absent in the narration of his gaze at the Topkapı Palace whilst sitting on a bench (156). The magnificent Galata Tower is depicted as “rising with a wizened pride [...] with its darkness which kept appearing and disappearing” (160). At various moments, historical heritage and artefacts enter the book as imagery illustrating the city as a ghost town: “a grand building in ruins and a five-hundred-year-old historic building was rendering this feeling of desolation even stronger” (20); a “defunct marble fountain with a dome which is not worth noticing despite its largeness” (192); “far away run-down fortifications, with their walls cracked, towers eroded or destroyed, would extend to the coast like a rusty saw” (67); “old structures of Galata with their plasters, ornaments fallen down” (98).

zh: 还应补充，在所有这些地方的描写中，无家可归者、流浪汉、吸胶者、卖纸巾的孩子和穷苦人，都是环境中的主要人物。各种乞丐纷纷出现，尤其在市中心；可怜的流浪动物也在画面之中。在小说中，盖奇金把伊斯坦布尔描绘为由丑陋、阴沉的边缘地带，以及混乱、阴郁的中心组成的城市。这些描写暗示了所谓“美丽”的城市，在穷人、无家可归者，以及所有被推到城市边缘的人眼中是什么样子。广受赞誉的《漫步伊斯坦布尔》的合著者约翰·弗里利，将这座城市称为“世界上最丑陋的美丽城市”（1999，29）。在《在边缘》中，盖奇金不断突出这座美丽城市的丑陋。
en: It should also be added that in the descriptions of all these places the homeless, tramps, glue sniffers, children selling tissue paper or miserable people come to the fore as the dominant figures of the environment. Various kinds of beggars appear, especially in the city centre, and pathetic stray animals are also in the picture. In the novel, Geçgin depicts Istanbul as a city comprising an ugly and sombre periphery, and a chaotic and grim centre. These depictions imply the way the ‘beautiful’ city appears for the poor, the homeless and all those who are pushed out to the periphery of the city. John Freely, the co-author of the acclaimed
describes this city as “the ugliest beautiful city of the world” (1999, 29). In
, Geçgin constantly accentuates the ugliness of this beautiful city.

zh: 塔什勒巴的生活

盖奇金从多个方面处理城市空间中的生活。市政服务的缺乏与基础设施问题，主要作为意象而非主题进入小说。作品广泛运用视觉与嗅觉意象，使人注意到这个被市政当局忽视的地方的处境。例如，下面这句话对塔什勒巴的描述：“他走过［……］沿街沟渠中流淌的泥水，从一个洞里钻出来、又消失在另一个洞里的老鼠，臭味，像雾一样落下的浓厚尘埃，灰暗［……］，走进旅店”（49）；又如对居兹科南污水气味（79）以及塔什勒巴下水道老鼠（130）的提及。这仅仅是几个例子。有一处，对污水的提及紧接在海滨散步区的描写之后（150）。塔什勒巴公园出口处有一条地下通道，被描述为：“地下通道［……］弥漫着粪便的臭味，仿佛整个地区、整座城市都散发着同样的气味”（45）。这里可能存在双重含义：整个地区都这样臭，整座城市也如此，因为对这部分城市的居民来说，他们居住的街区就意味着整座城市；或者，它可能暗示整座城市都是这个味道，也许是在隐喻意义上。
en: Geçgin addresses life in the urban space in a multifaceted manner. The lack of municipal services and infrastructural problems enter the novel mainly through imagery, rather than as themes. There is an extensive use of visual and olfactory imagery in the novel for drawing attention to the condition of this place neglected by the municipality. The description of Taşlıbağ in this sentence: “he was walking past [...] muddy waters running through the gutters alongside the street, mice that were coming out from one hole and disappearing in another, the smell, the dense dust that was falling down like fog, greyness [...] and entering the inn” (49); or the reference to the smell of the sewage waters in Güzkonan (79) and the sewage rats in Taşlıbağ (130) are only a couple of examples. At one moment, a reference to the sewage appears directly after the depiction of the strolling area beside the shore (150). In Taşlıbağ, at the exit of the park, there is an underpass which is described as follows: “the underpass [...] smelled of faeces, as if the whole quarter, all of this city smelled the same way” (45). Here, it is possible to find a double meaning. This entire area smells this way and so does the entire city: because for the dwellers of this part of the city, the neighbourhood they live in means the whole city; or it might imply that the whole city smells this way, perhaps metaphorically.

zh: 如上所述，塔什勒巴再现了卡兹勒切什梅。图尔盖·格克钦指出，“1945年，人们在泽伊廷布尔努的卡兹勒切什梅发现了伊斯坦布尔第一间棚屋”（2011，196）。到1947年，这一区域成为伊斯坦布尔第一个棚户聚居地（Akbulut 2011，210）。在整部小说中，棚户住房都是当时迁入者的常态。对于居利斯坦与比纳利这样的乡村迁入者，拥有自己的棚屋，被现实地描绘为一项目标：“全家人这样干了很久，积攒了多年的钱，终于得到了他们最看重的东西，像其他迁到城市的人一样达成目标；他们成了屋主，在上面某个街区买下一所小房子”（82）。正如凯末尔·卡尔帕特强调的，棚户区是城市中的“‘乡村’飞地”（2009，36）。与租房相比，住在自己的房子里，会使人对存在世界主义团结感的棚户区产生更强的依恋，因而也对城市产生更强的依恋。
en: As explained above, Taşlıbağ is a representation of Kazlıçeşme. As Turgay Gökçen acknowledges, “the first shanty in Istanbul was spotted in Kazlıçeşme, Zeytinburnu in 1945” (2011, 196). By 1947, the area became the first shanty settlement in Istanbul (Akbulut 2011, 210). Throughout the novel, shanty housing appears as the norm for migrants of the time. To have a shanty of one’s own is depicted, realistically, as an objective for rural migrants such as Gülistan and Binali: “The whole house having worked for a long time this way, having saved up money for years, have achieved the thing they valued the most, have accomplished their goal just like others who have migrated to the city, they have become homeowners, bought a small house in one of the neighbourhoods in the upper part” (82). As Kemal Karpat emphasises, the shanty town was a “‘rural’ enclave in the city” (2009, 36). Living in one’s own house rather than a rented one would result in a stronger attachment to the shanty town, where a sense of cosmopolitan solidarity is present, and therefore to a stronger attachment to the city.

zh: 在小说中，盖奇金对作为栖身之所的棚屋持积极态度，认为它们因带有花园而与自然相和谐。另一方面，对于以牟利为目的的公寓楼取代了棚屋的旧棚户区，他强调半建成楼房的丑陋与基础设施的缺乏。主人公眼中的自己街区就是这样的地方，简直不堪入目。如果棚户区转变后还留有世界主义的团结，他也丝毫感受不到。他不与同街区居民交往；街区对他而言显然不是一个飞地。他在街区中孤立，在城市中也孤立。他的个体性似乎是以隔绝为代价获得的。
en: In the novel, Geçgin has a positive approach to shanties as shelter, perceiving them to be in harmony with nature owing to their gardens. On the other hand, he accentuates the ugliness of the semi-built buildings and lack of infrastructure in former shanty towns where apartment buildings for profit have replaced the shanty houses. For the protagonist his neighbourhood is one such place, simply an eyesore. He does not feel any cosmopolitan solidarity, if there is any left after the transformation of shanty towns. He does not socialise with fellow inhabitants of the neighbourhood, which is certainly not an enclave for him. He is isolated in the neighbourhood, and he is isolated in the city. His individuality seems to be gained at the expense of isolation.

zh: 如前所述，过去与现在的塔什勒巴都出现在小说中。过去作为工业区的塔什勒巴，被描述为“一个只有男工人的巨大街区”；“一个与他们傍晚回去的房子、街区，或有些周末前去走访、散步的外部世界迥然不同的地方”（22）。工厂之外的生活就是“外部世界”。在这样的工作条件下，与外部世界极少接触，就意味着与城市生活极少接触。工人的个体化只是遥远的可能；下面这段关于在库姆卡帕或托兹卡帕候车的作坊工人的描写，暗示了这一点：“他们与多年前塔什勒巴皮革工厂的工人，或者与如今汇聚在乔尔卢、盖布泽的工厂里的工人，一模一样；这些人生活在工厂周围、由军事地区管控的聚居区中。他们有着同样的面孔、同样的姿态，仿佛一个模子，复制出越来越多的人”（25）。叙述者把工人描述为“一个无法区分的群体，由劳动着、并且仅仅为劳动而存在的身体组成”（25）。这里没有提及阶级；工人不是具有改变经济制度潜能的无产阶级成员。相反，叙述者以近乎冷嘲的方式，把他们比作机器人；在他看来，工人“只有劳动时才存在，而为了存在，他们必须劳动”（25）。这种机械的存在方式、阶级意识的缺乏，以及与城市生活的脱节之间，似乎存在关联：“他们在工厂工作，乘火车回家，睡觉，第二天早上起床，来上班，完成同一个循环［……］；他们以外那个巨大的世界，既不够有意义，也不够重要，更不够确定”（25）。大卫·哈维解释，奥斯曼如何“有意安排，把工人阶级的大部分以及其他不服管束的群体迁出［巴黎］市中心，因为他们在那里对公共秩序和政治权力构成威胁”（2008，33）。盖奇金没有讨论这一事实，他只是暗示工人与市中心的脱节，却没有表达看法：如果工人阶级身处市中心，会有什么不同？“他们以外那个巨大的世界”，就会变得“有意义”“重要”或“确定”吗？书中没有答案。
en: As mentioned above, both the former and the current Taşlıbağ appear in the novel. The former Taşlıbağ as an industry area is described as “a vast neighbourhood comprising only male workers”; “a place very different from the houses, neighbourhoods they return to in the evening or the outside world where they go on some weekends to visit and have a stroll” (22). The life outside of the factory is the “outside world”. Minimum contact with the outside world under these working conditions means minimum contact with urban life. Individualisation of workers is a remote possibility implied in the following depiction of workshop workers waiting for the train in Kumkapı or Tozkapı: “they were identical with workers in the leather factories in Taşlıbağ years ago or with those workers who work in the factories which have now come together in Çorlu or Gebze, living in their ghettoes established around factories under the control of military areas. With the same faces, same postures they were multiplying as if one and the same” (25). The narrator describes the workers as “an indistinguishable mass consisting of bodies working and existing only to work” (25). There is no reference to class here, workers are not members of the proletariat with the potential to change the economic system. On the contrary, in an almost cynical manner the narrator compares them to robots; according to him the workers “existed as long as they worked, and to exist they had to work” (25). There seems to be a correlation between this mechanical way of existence, a lack of class consciousness, and a disconnection from urban life: “they were working in the factory, taking the train and coming back home, sleeping, the next morning waking up and coming to work, completing the same cycle [...] a huge world other than theirs was neither meaningful, nor significant nor certain enough” (25). David Harvey explains how Haussman “deliberately engineered the removal of much of the working class and other unruly elements from the city centre [of Paris], where they constituted a threat to public order and political power” (2008, 33). Geçgin does not address this fact, he simply implies the disconnection of workers from the city centre but does not express an opinion on what would be different if the working class were at the city centre. Would “a huge world other than theirs” be “meaningful” or “significant” or “certain”? There is no answer to that in the book.

zh: 卡尔·马克思解释说：“［工人］在自身之外、与自身相对立地创造出来的异己的对象世界越强大，他自身——他的内在世界——就越贫乏，属于他自己所有的东西就越少”（2009，29）。小说中，工人将工厂称为“半开放监狱”（32），令人印象深刻地描述了这一过程。下面这段解释也具有类似意味：“孩子们在小型机器后面开始当学徒［……］，几年后就会到织机后面去，一直待到生命终结”（29）。
en: Karl Marx explains that “the more powerful becomes the alien world of objects which [the worker] creates over and against himself, the poorer he himself – his inner world – becomes, the less belongs to him as his own” (2009, 29). In the novel, workers’ definition of factories as a “semi-open prison” (32) is an impressive description of this process. A similar connotation can be found in the following explanation as well: “children who would start working as apprentices behind small machines [...] would then go behind looms after a couple of years and would stay there until the end of their lives” (29).

zh: 叙述者解释，在皮革工厂里，“独臂哈桑、缺指韦利、瘸子苏莱曼这样的绰号非常普遍”（29），由此表现了工作条件的残酷以及工人对此的默然承受。对皮革作坊与工厂（26—29、51），以及纺织作坊（76）的描写，是小说中生动而令人印象深刻的段落，以精细的细节呈现无产阶级生活的现实图景。
en: The harshness of the working conditions and workers’ acquiescence before it finds expression as the narrator explains that in the leather factories “nicknames such as Armless Hasan, Fingerless Veli, Cripple Süleyman were very common” (29). The depictions of the leather workshops and factories (26–29, 51) and textile workshops (76) stand out in the novel as vivid and impressive passages containing realistic pictures of proletarian life rendered in fine detail.

zh: 塔什勒巴的去工业化，是区分过去与现在的核心标志之一；卡兹勒切什梅工厂的拆除，通过一段令人心酸的文字进入作品。在阅读这段之前，不妨简要回顾历史背景。
en: The deindustrialisation of Taşlıbağ is one of the central markers of the difference between the past and the present; and the demolition of the Kazlıçeşme factories enters the book in a poignant passage. Before looking at this passage, it might be useful to briefly remember the historical context.

zh: 到20世纪40年代末，卡兹勒切什梅已经成为工业街区；1949年，它被正式宣布为“重工业区”（Akbulut 2011，207）。1955至1973年间，这一区域建立了325家皮革行业的工厂与作坊（208）。按照1982年的规划，这些工厂在80年代末开始迁往图兹拉，从而结束了这一地区长达五百年的皮革工业史（209）。该区域剩余工厂的最后拆除发生在1993年（Kürkçüoğlu 2020）。
en: Kazlıçeşme had become an industrial neighbourhood by the end of the 1940s, and in 1949 it was officially announced as a “heavy industry area” (Akbulut 2011, 207). From 1955 to 1973, 325 factories and workshops in the leather sector were established in this area (208). In line with a plan dated to 1982, by the end of the 1980s these factories started to be transferred to Tuzla, which brought an end to the 500-year-long history of the leather industry in the area (209). The final demolition of the remaining factories in the area was in 1993 (Kürkçüoğlu 2020).

zh: 在相关段落中，主人公沿着历史城墙行走，直到塔什勒巴最后残存的一条街道。他在那里看到一栋只剩外墙的建筑废墟。他发现，无家可归者如今住在里面，搭起塑料屋顶，搬来一把椅子和一张桌子，用石头垒了炉灶。他继续行走，废墟意象愈发强烈：“［他］走在路上，两侧满是残骸、石堆与尘土，耳中的呼啸声越来越高”（129）。眼前是一片广阔空地，他继续行走，试图把握被城市改造抹去的城市记忆：“一种渴望从沙沙作响的草丛中升起，他试着回忆旅店从前的位置、入口、工厂间铺满皮革粉尘的狭窄街巷、店铺的位置，以及茶馆”（129）。他回想起街坊们当初如何好奇地期待拆除：“那件说了许多年的事［……］，以不可思议的速度完成了；机器只用几星期就拆完了。除了石头与下水道老鼠，什么也没有留下”（130）。广阔的空地是这段中有力的母题，强调街区历史被粗暴地切断。该地区的去工业化抹去了工人阶级文化，而拆除又抹去了它的记忆。应当指出，卡兹勒切什梅皮革工厂拆除后留下的空间，本来打算用作休闲区，却从未被市政当局妥善改造成这一用途（Akbulut 2011，209）。
en: In the related passage, the protagonist walks by the historical city walls until he arrives at the last remaining street of Taşlıbağ. There he sees the ruin of a building with only the outer walls remaining. He observes that the homeless now live in this building having put a plastic roof on top, brought a chair and a table, and made a stove from stones. The imagery of ruins is intensified as he continues his walk: “[he] was walking on the road, both sides of which were covered in debris, piles of stones and dust, with the howl in his ears ascending” (129). With a vast empty space in front of him he continues walking, trying to grasp the memory of the city erased by urban transformation: “with a desire rising from the rustling grass, he was trying to recall the former site of the inn, entrance gateway, narrow streets covered in leather dust between factories, the site of the shops, the tea house” (129). He remembers how the demolition was expected by the neighbourhood dwellers with curiosity: “The thing talked about for many long years [...] was over and done with at an unbelievable speed, the demolition was completed with machines in a couple of weeks. Nothing was left behind, except stones and sewer rats” (130). The vast empty space is a powerful motif in the passage, stressing the harsh severing of the history of the neighbourhood. The deindustrialisation of the area wipes away the working-class culture, while the demolition erases the memory of it. It should be noted that the space in Kazlıçeşme left after the demolition of the leather factories, which was intended to be utilised as a recreation area, has never been properly transformed for such a purpose by the municipality (Akbulut 2011, 209).

zh: 在城中闲荡

在书中，边缘既是场景，也是意象，个人的孤立与被隔绝于城市边缘的主题由此交织。主人公是个闲荡者。年少时，他常与舅舅伊斯一起闲荡：“他们出发上路，像游魂一样在城里闲荡”（79）。主人公从伊斯那里学会闲荡；伊斯在外面总是很自在：“伊斯走得放松、挺直、自信，仿佛街道都属于他，每走一步，身体都向一侧倾斜”（86）。伊斯不工作，周围人似乎也接受他本来的样子。在他们歇脚的茶园或啤酒馆，伊斯认识店主或服务员。伊斯与主人公在人群中不停地走，直到筋疲力尽，停在公园里：“伊斯［……］在公园里如在家中”（65）。他们在所住的因吉尔柯伊及其周边街道闲荡，也在海岸、茶园与啤酒馆闲荡。有时乘小巴去居兹科南探亲，有时去巴克尔库莱。与伊斯闲荡的这些记忆，构成主人公童年与少年记忆的主要部分。在故事的当下，他独自闲荡。然而，这种闲荡有别于
en: In the book, the themes of personal isolation and being isolated on the periphery of the city get enmeshed as the periphery acts both as a setting and imagery. The protagonist is an idler. When he was younger he used to idle with his uncle İs: “they were hitting the road to idle like a spirit inside the city” (79). The protagonist learns idling from İs who is always comfortable outside: “İs was walking relaxed, straight, confident, as if the streets belonged to him, with his body leaning to the side with each step” (86). İs does not work, and those around him seem to accept İs the way he is. He knows the owners or waiters in the tea gardens or beer houses where they take their breaks. İs and the protagonist walk endlessly in the crowds until they are exhausted and stop in a park: “İs [...] felt at home in the park” (65). They idle in the streets in and around İncirköy where they live, on the coast, in tea gardens and beer houses there. They sometimes take the minibus to Güzkonan to visit their relatives, and sometimes go to Bakırkule. These memories of idling with İs dominate the childhood and adolescent memories of the protagonist. In the present time he idles solo. However, this idling is different from

zh: 《在边缘》的主人公是一个孤立的人，似乎正经历着西曼所说的以“孤立”形式出现的异化（1959，789）。这种孤立及伴随的抑郁感刻画了他的内心世界：“他感到深深的悲伤，却不知道原因”（170）。他觉得自己与家人、亲属，与那些大多被描绘为勤劳且充满活力的工人阶级成员（25、32），以及与城市本身都脱了节：“他觉得自己像被流放在陌生土地上的人”（144）。这一描写既可能发挥字面作用，也可能发挥隐喻作用。然而，尽管感到流亡，他仍在长时间的城市步行中寻求庇护。很难把这些长途步行称为
：泰斯特在讨论穆齐尔时描述的那些使
走向终结的因素，在这里以强烈得多的方式存在。交通、城市神秘感的消失，以及“理性”与“秩序”的霸权，在穆齐尔笔下20世纪的维也纳与
相抵触（Tester 2006，13）；而在盖奇金笔下21世纪的伊斯坦布尔，它们以极端程度存在。盖奇金在整部小说中指出这一事实，把闲荡母题与作为城市权利的休闲空间和活动的可及性主题联系起来。
en: The protagonist of

is an isolated figure, who seems to be experiencing what Seeman describes as alienation in the form of “isolation” (1959, 789). His inner world is characterised through this isolation and concomitant depressive feelings: “he was feeling a deep sadness, the reason for which he didn’t know” (170). He feels disconnected from his family and relatives, from the working class whose members are portrayed mostly as hard-working people full of life (25, 32), and from the city as well: “he was feeling like someone in exile in an unfamiliar land” (144). Such a depiction might function both on a literal and a metaphorical level. Despite this feeling of exile, however, he takes refuge in his long strolls in the city. It is difficult to describe these long walks as
: what Tester describes with reference to Musil as factors bringing
to its end are present here in a much more intense way. Traffic, loss of the urban enigma and the hegemony of “rationality” and “order” that are against

in Musil’s Vienna of the twentieth century (Tester 2006, 13) are present, in extreme proportions, in Geçgin’s Istanbul of the twenty-first century. Pointing out this fact throughout the novel, Geçgin links the motif of idling with the theme of access to recreational areas and activities as a right to the city.

zh: 公园与海岸不断出现在书中，成为逃离城市阴郁、也在一定程度上逃离存在恐惧的庇护所（45、96—97、125、144、150）。主人公与伊斯经常走到自己街区的公园里。那里的一点自然气息对伊斯意义重大，他称其为“生活中最好的东西”（65）。因吉尔柯伊附近的海岸线，也是小说的重要场景：那里有茶园和啤酒馆，也可以散步（68）。同样，巴克尔库莱的主广场是两人闲荡时的重要地点：“快到巴克尔库莱，他们便下车。他们走过广场，走过拥挤的人群、坐在水泥长椅上晒太阳的人、在阴凉处寻求清爽的人、倚着柱子或树站着的人、在广场上闲荡的人，汇入午后外出购物或漫无目的游逛的人流，沿着拱廊、杂志和商店排列的街道，向海边走去”（85）。文本清楚表明，城市空间并未给他们提供活动或社会交往机会，只是提供了四处走动的场所。
en: Parks and shores keep appearing in the book as a shelter from the grimness of the city and to a certain extent from existential fear (45, 96– 97, 125, 144, 150). The protagonist and İs very often find themselves in the park in their neighbourhood. The touch of nature there means a lot to İs who calls it “the best thing in life” (65). The coastline close to İncirköy is also a significant setting in the novel: there are tea gardens and beer houses, and it is also possible to stroll (68). Similarly, the main square of Bakırkule is an important location for the pair as they are idling: “They were getting off as they come close to Bakırkule. They were walking past the square, those who crowd in the square, sitting on concrete benches in the sunshine, those seeking freshness in the shade, those who stand leaning on a column or a tree, those idling in the square, joining the afternoon crowd who are out for shopping or wandering aimlessly, and walking down the street where arcades, magazines, shops line up towards the seaside” (85). As is clear in the text, the urban space does not offer them activities or opportunities for socialisation, but simply offers spaces to wander around.

zh: 小说第一部第五章以一段长文开篇，描述古城墙周边以及供野餐的小片绿地（125—126）。叙述者还补充说，附近山坡是流浪汉与无家可归者夜间睡觉的地方。城市中出现的小片自然，是生活在边缘地带的贫困迁入者的绿洲。在不欢迎他们的市中心，公园和海滨这些公共空间，是无力负担休闲活动者唯一可去的地方。在最后几章的场景中，盖齐公园与马奇卡公园占据突出位置，主人公用两天时间，从卡拉柯伊一路步行到埃米诺努。小说这一部分对马奇卡公园的描写，鲜明地表现了公园在低收入居民缺乏休闲机会的大都市中所发挥的作用：“来公园的通常是后街、希什利的贫困街区以及更远地方的人，尤其周末，他们把公园填满［……］；那些无法进室内坐坐的人，没钱看电影的穷人，都在这里闲逛。不论在哪里，公园都属于他们”（184）。他随后补充：“贫困街区的年轻男女来这里约会，在这里相见。无家可归者待在这里，只要警察没发现、没把他们赶走，或者对他们视而不见。失业者在这里度过白天”（184）。这部小说写于2013年盖齐公园抗议之前。
在这些引文中，看到那个历史时刻的预兆，令人震动：全球化城市中经济地租的创造，导致公园遭到侵占，而公园是城市里唯一欢迎穷人的空间。还应指出，小说中伊斯与主人公闲荡的泽伊廷布尔努沿海多个地点，在过去十年间已被建筑公司占据。
en: The fifth chapter of the first book of the novel starts with a long passage describing the area around the old city walls, the small patches of green used as a picnic area (125–126). The narrator also adds that in the hills near this area, tramps and the homeless sleep at night. Small tracts of nature appearing within the city are oases for poor migrants living on the periphery. In the unwelcoming city centre, the public spaces of parks and the seaside are the only sites for those who cannot afford recreation activities. Gezi Park and Maçka Park have a prominent place in the setting of the final chapters, as the protagonist takes a long walk over two days from Karaköy to Eminönü. The description of Maçka Park in this part of the novel is a perfect manifestation of the function of parks in a metropolis where the opportunities for recreational activities are scarce for low-income inhabitants: “Usually people from back quarters, from poor neighbourhoods of Şişli, from further away were coming to the park, they were filling the park especially at weekends [...] those who can’t go indoors to sit down, broke people who can’t go to the cinema, poor people were hanging around here. Parks wherever they are belonged to them” (184). He then adds: “Young boys and girls from poor neighbourhoods came here for their dates, they met each other here. The homeless stayed here as long as the police did not spot them and send them away, or if they ignored them. The unemployed spent their daytime here” (184). This novel was written before the Gezi Park Protests of 2013.

It is striking to see in the lines quoted above a foreshadowing of that historical moment: the economic rent creation in the globalising city leads to the invasion of parks, the only space in the urban area that welcomes the poor. It should also be noted that various points of the shore in Zeytinburnu area, where İs and the protagonist idle in the novel, have been occupied by building companies in the last decade.

zh: 如上一节所述，叙述者形容因吉尔柯伊位于“一个并不存在的中心的边缘”（12）。下面的引文也清楚地强调了这座没有中心的城市：
en: As mentioned in the previous section, the narrator describes İncirköy as located “at the periphery of a non-existent centre” (12). This emphasis on the city without a centre is clear in the following extract as well:

zh: 又或者，在公共假日，成百上千的少年离开自己的地盘，去塔克西姆或城市其他中心地带，享受城市生活的恩惠；在空荡荡的市中心，他们遇见与自己相似的人，便径直折返，从于克塞克卡尔德勒姆走下去，混进埃米诺努令人发狂的人潮。没有什么地方可去，也没有什么东西可达。没有城市中心。也许连城市都没有。（12—13）
en: Or on a public holiday, leaving their own turf, hundreds of teenagers were going to Taksim or another central part of the city to benefit from the blessings of urban life, in a deserted city centre encountering those similar to themselves, they were turning right back, going down from Yüksek Kaldırım and mixing with the maddening crowd of Eminönü. There was neither a place nor a thing to reach. There was no city centre. Maybe there was even no city. (12–13)

zh: 边缘地区的居民前往城市中心区域时，遇到与自己相似的人，却彼此没有互动。他们怀着体验城市社会生活的期待与愿望前往市中心，上面的引文把这称为“享受城市生活的恩惠”。这些“城市恩惠”是什么？边缘地区的少年去塔克西姆这样的地方，会期待什么？他们大概期待与同龄城市居民交往，建立友谊，或彼此调情。他们期待愉快地散步、坐坐咖啡馆，观看体育比赛，或许亲自参与，在电影院看电影；对文化活动感兴趣的人，则期待看戏或听音乐会。引文强调，边缘居民不可能这样融入城市文化。而这种融入，是一种城市权利。在理想的城市环境中，即使只有少量零花钱用于娱乐的少年，也应能够负担上述大部分活动，这些活动应通过城市公共设施得到提供。青少年应有社会休闲中心及类似场所，可以参与体育或文化艺术，或在俱乐部里找到培养爱好的空间。这些场所也会成为与其他少年交往的地方。上面的引文表明，缺少这样的社会／福利组织，市中心就成了一片空洞；这或许正是叙述者形容中心“并不存在”的原因。城市中心的缺席，几乎被等同于城市本身的缺席：如果无法参与城市的社会文化生活，就无从感受城市的存在。
en: Inhabitants of the periphery in their visit to a central area of the city encounter those who are similar to them, but there is no interaction between them. They go to the city centre with the expectation of and desire for experiencing urban social life, described in the above excerpt as “to benefit from the blessings of urban life”. What are these “urban blessings”? What would teenagers from the periphery expect when they go to a place like Taksim? They would probably expect to socialise with city inhabitants of their age, for friendship and for flirtation. They would expect to spend a pleasant time strolling around, sitting in a cafe, to watch a sports match or maybe participate in one, to see a movie in a cinema, and for those who are interested in cultural activities, see a play or a concert. The extract underlines the impossibility of such an integration of the dwellers of the periphery with urban culture. Such integration is a right to the city. In an ideal urban setting, even teenagers who have a small amount of pocket money to spend on pleasure could afford most of the activities listed above, made available through urban amenities. Social recreation centres and similar areas would be available for the youth, where they could get involved in sports or culture and arts, or find space for hobbies in clubs. These would also serve as a venue to socialise with other teenagers. The extract above indicates that in the absence of such social/welfare organisations the city centre becomes a void, which might be the reason why the narrator describes the centre as “non-existing”. The absence of a city centre is almost equated with the absence of a city: there is no way of feeling the presence of the city if one cannot be a part of its social and cultural life.

zh: 关于生活在城市边缘的贫困居民处境的段落，叙述声音乍听可能中立，对他们毫不同情。但事实并非如此。叙述声音中可见的，并非外部人用怜悯话语表达的同情，而是内部人的愤懑；“离开自己的地盘”“径直折返”这样的用词，正表现了这一点。
en: The narrative voice in the passage on the position of poor inhabitants of the city living on the periphery might at first sound neutral and without any sympathy for them. But this is not the case. Rather than an outsider’s sympathy expressed in words of compassion, the resentment of an insider is visible in the narrative voice, manifest in word choices such as “leaving their own turf” or “turning right back”.

zh: 在故事的当下，主人公在全球化进程中的伊斯坦布尔闲荡。由此产生的多元文化，在下面这段关于中心旅游区卡拉柯伊的文字中，几乎呈现为一幅幻景：“他一头扎进声音的河流：有人在铺在地上的布上卖小饰品、皮革制成的小物件、鸟巢（这些人通常来自被称作突厥诸共和国的地方），还有钟表、香水、小雕像、面具（卖这些的通常是来自非洲的年轻人），有人卖外国香烟、来自凡城或乌尔法的手卷烟草，混杂在吆喝声、说话声、尖叫声、船的汽笛声和渡轮声中”（102）。这是一座迁移已不再局限于国内乡城迁移的城市；它也接收来自国外的移民。下面这段话清楚地强调了这一点：“街道上，俄罗斯、摩尔多瓦或罗马尼亚女人，在下等夜总会和酒吧工作、住在民宿或出租房里的年轻男孩，妓女、闲荡者、阿拉伯人、黑人、找各种活干的人、酒鬼、小偷、流氓、小贩，以及从全国各地迁来的人，都在走动”（107）。在小说中，多元文化似乎又为城市固有的混乱增添了一层。在描写主人公于加拉塔观察广场、游客从旁经过的这段文字中，盖奇金还提到了绅士化：
en: In the story’s current time, the protagonist is idling in the globalising Istanbul. The resulting multiculturalism appears almost as a phantasmagoria in the following passage on the central and touristic area of Karaköy: “he was diving into a river of sound, made up of those selling little ornaments on the cloth they spread out on the floor, little objects made of leather, birds’ nests (these were usually from the place called the Turki Republics), clocks, perfume, little statues, masks (and these were usually youngsters from Africa), those selling foreign cigarettes, hand-rolled tobacco from Van or Urfa, amid bellows, voices talking, screams, ships’ horns, ferry noises” (102). This is a city where migration is no longer limited to internal rural–urban migration; it receives external migration as well. The emphasis on this is clear in the following excerpt: “in the streets, Russian, Moldavian, or Romanian women, young boys working in lowlife nightclubs and bars, and staying in bed & breakfasts or rented rooms, prostitutes, idlers, Arabs, Blacks, those looking for any kind of a job, alcoholics, thieves, hoodlums, vendors, those who have migrated from every part of the country were walking around” (107). In the novel, multiculturalism appears to be an addition to the chaos inherent in the city. There is also a reference to gentrification in the passage as Geçgin depicts the protagonist in Galata, observing the square as tourists pass by:

zh: 楼房向上伸展，灰泥剥落，浮雕褪色；它们一间间出租，被用作店铺、作坊或仓库，多子女家庭住在里面。演员、画家、音乐家、记者、历史场所爱好者、有些钱的人、外国人——这些整夜在酒吧里混的人，也在这一带租房、买房，于是街区就像一幅活动起来的阿拉伯图画，所有图案杂乱地交织在一起。（160）
en: Upwards stretched buildings whose plaster had fallen off, and reliefs had faded, that were rented room by room, used as shops, workshops or depots, where families with many children lived. Actors and actresses, painters, musicians, journalists, lovers of historical places, moderately rich ones, foreigners, who fool around in bars all night long were also renting, buying houses around here, thus the neighbourhood was like an animated Arabic picture where all motifs enmeshed in a disordered way. (160)

zh: 虽然绅士化只在这一段中被提及，却是城市在20世纪90年代所经历转型的一个重要标志。
en: Although gentrification is addressed only in this passage, it is an important indicator of the transformation the city is going through in the 1990s.

zh: 《在边缘》把闲荡的母题巧妙地同无家可归背景下的住房权主题联系起来。除了伊斯这样没有稳定工作、却有家的闲荡者，小说中也出现了无处可住的闲荡者。他们或者还能找到临时落脚之处，或者彻底无家可归、流落街头；在城市的描写中，他们随时都会出人意料地出现，例如：“无家可归者、被排斥的人，或者自身就仿佛某种垃圾的疯人”（11）；“一个有几个无家可归者冻死的冬天［……］过去了”（146）；“海岸上，除了几个晨行的人和睡在长椅上的无家可归者，空无一人”（149）。在小说中，闲荡者与无家可归者之间的界线似乎很薄，尤其对那些迁入城市、又缺乏亲属关系支持网络的人而言：“无家可归者栖身于废弃旅店、破败房间；失业者、做零工的落魄者、初来城市的人，住在廉价肮脏的旅馆和出租房里”（161）。在小说第二部中，主人公遇到一位过去的熟人。此人名叫恩金，“看经济状况，或住公寓，或住单间，或住旅馆”（164）。主人公请他吃午饭。恩金谈起自己离开伊斯坦布尔的打算时，“一个用头巾遮脸的乞讨女人”（166）被从餐馆门口赶走。恩金抱怨这座城市，说自己再也待不下去了，并提起几天前遭到袭击的事，作为这里多么糟糕的例证。他又说：“我要回老家”（167）。离开时，他开口借钱，好付所住旅馆的房费。这段约三页半长的文字，使焦点拉近到书中一个濒临彻底无家可归的闲荡者的故事上：一个被城市拒绝、无法在其中维生的人，除了回乡之外别无选择。
en: In

, the motif of idling is skilfully tied to the theme of the right to housing in the context of homelessness. In addition to idlers like İs, without a steady job but with a home, idlers without a place to live are also visible in the novel. They are either men who are able to find temporary places to stay, or those completely homeless living in the streets; they keep appearing unexpectedly in the depictions of the city at any moment, as in the following examples: “the homeless, outcasts, or lunatics who were themselves a sort of garbage” (11); “a winter in which a couple of the homeless had frozen to death [...] has passed” (146); “on the coast there was no-one except for a couple of early walkers and the homeless sleeping on the benches” (149). In the novel, the line between being an idler and a homeless person seems to be very thin, especially for those who have migrated to the city and lack a network support based on kinship relations: “the homeless were taking shelter in deserted inns, dilapidated rooms; the unemployed, fallen ones doing temporary jobs, those who are new to the city were staying in cheap, dingy hotels and rented rooms” (161). In the second book of the novel, the protagonist encounters an acquaintance from the past. This person, named Engin, stays “either in a flat, in a room or at a hotel depending on his financial situation” (164). The protagonist treats him to lunch. As Engin talks about his plans to leave Istanbul, “a beggar woman covering her face with a scarf” (166) gets expelled from the door of the diner. Engin complains about the city, says that he cannot stay there any longer, and mentions an event of assault he experienced a couple of days before, as an example of how terrible a place it is. He adds: “I will go back to my hometown” (167). As he leaves, he asks for money to pay for the room in the hotel he is staying at. This passage, about three and a half pages long, appears as a way of bringing the focus closer to the story of one of the idlers in the novel who is on the verge of being completely homeless: a person who is rejected by the city, has no means to survive in it, so does not have any other option than going back to his hometown.

zh: 在这幅充满城市贫困、失业、排斥与无家可归现象的城市图景中，乞丐、卖纸巾的孩子和吸胶者也不断出现。无论是主要着眼过去的第一部，还是以当下为背景的第二部，都有这些人的身影。主人公在漫长步行途中，曾停在加拉塔塔脚下的一处茶园；对那里一个寻常下午的描写，将所有这些彼此纠缠的问题汇聚在一起，因而值得注意：“在那小小的空地上，一群吸胶的孩子拿着捡来的破球踢比赛。他们大多站在原地踢球，像梦游者一样，斜着眼踢向滚到脚边的球，不时闻一闻攥成拳头的手掌里”（159）。叙述者又说：“摆摊的孩子和乞丐追着旅游团。稍远处，几个孩子躺在长椅上望着天空；几个失业者在睡觉”（159—160）。傍晚，他继续沿独立大街行走：“卖纸巾、口香糖或鲜花的孩子，还有擦鞋童，走来走去；商店前、门前，没有手臂的、没有脚的、盲人、跛子、老人、脚肿的人、肢体畸形残缺的人、只剩半截身体的人、聋哑人、饥饿的人、患病的人和孩子，都在乞讨”（162—163）。有一次，在盖齐公园，主人公给了吸胶者一点零钱，随后又给了一个向他要钱的男人。另一次类似场景发生在马奇卡公园：一个吸胶男孩逗着一条狗玩，狗由它的上层阶级主人牵着散步。那人让男孩和狗玩了几分钟，随后粗鲁地叫他走开。于是男孩走到树下，继续远远地看着狗。主人公从他身边走过时，男孩讨一支烟；主人公给了他，继续走路（186—187）。在这类场景中，借用侯赛因·克兰的说法，叙述者以“金属般的语言”作出的描写，完全客观而中性。

读来仿佛这一切在大都市中都是寻常情形。正如格奥尔格·齐美尔解释的：“大都市类型的人［……］为自己创造出一个保护器官，以抵御外部环境的波动与不连续所带来的深刻扰乱。大都市类型的人主要以理性的方式作出反应，而非情感反应”（2002，12）。然而，这些段落的内容暗示，《在边缘》的无名主人公，并没有那么能免受齐美尔所说的“外部环境的波动与不连续”的影响。他同情那些被排斥的人，而大多数城市居民甚至不曾注意他们。正因为主人公具有这种同情，书中许多时刻都凸显了这类人物。
en: Beggars, children selling tissue paper and glue sniffers also keep appearing in the picture of this city of urban poverty, unemployment, exclusion and homelessness. All these appear both in the first book, which mostly focuses on the past, and the second book which is set in the present time. At one point on his long walk, the protagonist stops at a tea garden at the bottom of the Galata tower, and the depiction of an ordinary afternoon there is noteworthy for bringing together all these issues as they intertwine with each other: “In the small space, a group of glue-sniffer children were playing a football match with a burst ball they had found. Most of them were swinging at the ball where they stood, like a sleep-walker hitting the ball that comes to their feet with their cross-eyes, every now and again sniffing inside the palms of their hands made into fists” (159). He adds: “street vendor children and beggars were chasing tourist groups. A bit further away, a couple of children were looking at the sky lying on benches; a couple of unemployed people were sleeping” (159–160). He continues his walk on İstiklal Street at evening time: “Children selling tissue paper, chewing gum or flowers and shoeshine boys were walking around; in front of shops or doors, those without arms, feet, the blind, cripples, oldtimers, those with swollen feet, those with irregular, flawed organs, those with half bodies, deaf mutes, the hungry, the ill, and children were begging” (162–163). In one instance, in Gezi Park the protagonist gives some change to glue sniffers; and then a man who asks him for money. In another similar moment, the setting is Maçka Park, where a glue-sniffer boy plays with a dog who is being walked by its upper-class owner. After a couple of minutes of allowing the boy to play with his dog, the man rudely tells him to go away. So the boy goes under the trees and continues watching the dogs at a distance. As the protagonist walks by him, the boy asks for a cigarette, he gives it to him and continues walking (186–187). In such instances, in the “metallic language” of the narrator, to borrow Hüseyin Kıran’s description, depictions are purely objective and neutral.

They sound as if in a metropolis all these are ordinary instances. As Georg Simmel explains: “the metropolitan type [...] creates a protective organ for itself against the profound disruption with which the fluctuations and discontinuities of the external milieu threaten it. Instead of reacting emotionally, the metropolitan type reacts primarily in a rational manner” (2002, 12). However, the content of such passages implies that the nameless protagonist of
i

not that immune to what Simmel calls “the fluctuations and discontinuities of the external milieu”. He has compassion for outcasts, while the majority of urban inhabitants do not even notice them. Owing to this compassion of the protagonist, such figures are prominent at many moments of the book.

zh: 如上所述，小说标题可以译作“在边缘”。在作品中，边缘呈现出多个层次：第一层，是主人公处于存在之边缘的总体主题。另一层，是边缘更直接、更字面的存在：位于城市边缘的街区。正如阿米尔、芬奇和萨尔梅拉恰当指出的，“研究城市的边缘性时，学者应当‘始终采取相对的视角’，其中包含‘这样一种意识：视角的转移，可能使支配与从属的地理关系发生颠倒’”（2015，8）。事实上，《在边缘》出版仅十三年后，泽伊廷布尔努的边缘地位便已发生相当大的变化：随着城市不断扩张，这一区域一天天“接近”中心。还有一层，则如前述例子所示，是那些困在城市社会、经济和文化生活边缘的人进入了小说。盖奇金描绘这些人的方式，与瓦尔特·本雅明看待城市局外人的方式相契合。
en: As discussed above, the title of the novel can be translated as “on the periphery”. In the work, the periphery appears on various layers: on the first layer, there is the overall theme of the protagonist being on the periphery of existence. On another layer, there is a more direct and literal existence of periphery: the neighbourhoods which are on the periphery of the city. As Ameel, Finch and Salmela aptly observe, “when urban peripherality is considered, scholars should ‘always assume a relative perspective’, containing ‘the awareness that a shift in point of view may turn a geography of domination of subordination on its head’” (2015, 8). As a matter of fact, even thirteen years after the publication of

, Zeytinburnu’s peripheral status has changed considerably: as the city keeps expanding, this area ‘approaches’ the centre day by day. On yet another layer, as illustrated in the examples above, those who are stuck on the periphery of the social, economic and cultural life of the urban setting enter the novel. The way Geçgin illustrates these people is compatible with Walter Benjamin’s approach to outsiders in the city.

zh: 盖奇金向我们呈现了一张属于闲荡者、被排斥者、流浪汉和无家可归者的城市面孔。格雷姆·吉洛克清楚地解释，本雅明努力“为‘边缘者’发声，表达那些被现代秩序形式力图变成无声、不可见之人的经验”；他又补充：“闲步的

、自觉展示自我的花花公子、大声嚷叫的乞丐、受苦的妓女、悲惨的拾荒者：这些边缘的、受忽视的人物，栖居在本雅明书写城市的篇页之中”（1996，9）。吉洛克将本雅明的目标描述为“赋予边缘者和被压迫者力量”，而且“为此，这些城市景观提供了一种大都市环境中边缘人物的现象学。它们讲述儿童、妓女、乞丐、拾荒者及其他人的经验”（15）。这类“边缘的、受忽视的人物”在《在边缘》中始终存在。他们作为主导母题反复出现，把住房权、劳动权等问题带进了小说。
en: Geçgin presents us with a face of the city that belongs to idlers, outcasts, tramps and the homeless. Graeme Gilloch lucidly explains that Benjamin strives “to give voice to the ‘periphera’, the experience of those whom modern forms of order strive to render silent and invisible” and adds: “the sauntering

, the self-conscious dandy, the loud-mouthed beggar, the suffering prostitute, the wretched rag-picker: marginal, disregarded figures inhabit Benjamin’s pages on the city” (1996, 9). Gilloch describes Benjamin’s objective as “empower[ing] the marginal and the oppressed” and “to this end, the cityscapes offer a phenomenology of the marginal figures of the metropolitan environment. They relate the experiences of the child, the prostitute, the beggar, the rag-picker and others” (15). Such “marginal, disregarded figures” are constantly present in
. Their existence as a leitmotif brings issues such as the right to housing and the right to work to the pages of the novel.

zh: 结论

小说中有一处，叙述者强调主人公家族的村庄已经不复存在，因为留在那里的人全都迁到了镇上（116）。另一处，则把村庄描述为“要么自行空了，要么被清空了”（35）。主人公的祖父回村度过最后一个夏天，并葬在那里。这有力地象征着他与村庄、乡村背景、安纳托利亚土地的联系。对主人公的父亲而言，这同样具有象征意义：伊斯坦布尔不是他能够祭扫父亲坟墓的地方，而父亲的坟墓是根的隐喻。不过，他本人去世后却葬在伊斯坦布尔。因此，对主人公来说，伊斯坦布尔
他可以祭扫父亲坟墓的地方。这个细微的细节，动人地表现了城市在不同代际迁入者之间发生变化的象征意义。
en: At one point in the novel, the narrator stresses that the village of the protagonist’s family no longer exists, since all the remaining population there have moved to the town (116). In another instance, villages are described as “either emptied by themselves or were depopulated” (35). The protagonist’s grandfather spends his last summer back in his village and gets buried there. This is a powerful symbol of his ties with his village, with his rural background, with the Anatolian soil. It is also symbolic for the protagonist’s father: Istanbul is not the place where he can visit his father’s grave, a metaphor for roots. When he dies, however, he gets buried in Istanbul. So, for the protagonist, Istanbul
the place where he can visit his father’s grave. This subtle detail poignantly manifests the shifting symbolic meaning of the city between different generations of migrants.

zh: 主人公总会走到马奇卡公园：“他来来回回地走，最后发现自己又到了这座公园”（185）。如前所述，对于没有钱花在休闲上的城市居民，公园极为重要。小说中没有足够信息判断主人公是否也如此。然而，他与公园、绿地及大海的深厚联系，似乎暗示着多重动机。他对绿色的喜爱，在一定程度上可能意味着继承了父母的乡村背景；而城市绿地的缺乏，也可能是他疏离城市的原因之一。从这一角度看，末章中一段较长文字（179—182）里的盖齐公园，几乎预示了2013年的盖齐抗议——它发生于《在边缘》出版十年之后，是城市居民争取绿地权、也即城市权利的一个难忘时刻。
en: The protagonist always ends up in Maçka Park: “he was walking back and forth and eventually finding himself in this park” (185). As discussed earlier, for the city inhabitants who do not have money to spend for recreation, parks have great importance. There is not sufficient information in the novel as to whether this is also the case for the protagonist. However, his deep connection with parks, green spaces and the sea seem to imply a multidimensional motivation. His fondness for green might, to a certain extent, imply a heritage from the rural background of his parents; and the lack of green space in the city might be one of the reasons for his detachment from the city. In this respect, Gezi Park, which appears in a long passage (179–182) in the final chapter, appears almost as a foreshadowing of the Gezi Protests of 2013 which took place ten years after the publication of
: an unforgettable moment of urban inhabitants’ fight for their right to green space, in other words for their right to the city.

zh: 海是小说中重要的意象。它带有无限之感，召唤人对存在进行沉思。它也是多数居民都能享有的城市之美；只要坐在长椅上，或者沿海岸散步，就可以欣赏。小说以这一意象收尾：主人公坐在贝希克塔什港口，观察眼前景色。这是存在的沉思与城市日常生活相遇的时刻。一对情侣在长椅上相拥，三个人站在船边喝啤酒、低声交谈，另一头有个人在看海。如今，贝希克塔什港口旁的茶园已不复存在，由于总统接管了原先的市长办公楼，那里停满了警用巴士。院子里的公园，过去被贝希克塔什居民叫作市长公园，如今也不再向公众开放。购物中心和豪华酒店侵占城市最好的部分，那些曾经向所有人开放、供所有人享用的城市空间，一个接一个地消失；书中动人地表现了这些空间的形象。除了市政服务等基本需要，盖奇金还提醒人们关注作为城市权利的休闲场所与活动权。小说描绘了一幅全球化中的伊斯坦布尔的阴郁图景，读来如同对这一过程破坏性后果的警告。盖奇金把迁移、工人阶级生活、边缘街区、去工业化与无家可归的故事交织起来，透过居民未获承认的权利，呈现了新自由主义城市现实的一幅万花筒式图景。
en: The sea is a significant imagery in the novel. It carries a feeling of infinity, something which calls for contemplation on existence. It is also an accessible beauty of the city for most of its inhabitants; simply sitting on a bench or strolling on the shore makes it possible to enjoy it. The novel ends with that imagery, as the protagonist sits at the Beşiktaş harbour observing the scenery. This is a moment when contemplation of existence meets with daily life in the city. There is a couple sitting on a bench holding each other, three people are having their beers and speaking in whispers as they stand by the boats, and at the other end there is one person watching the sea. Today the tea gardens next to the Beşiktaş harbour are no longer there, and the area is full of police buses, since the president took over the former mayoral office there. The park in its yard, which used to be called the Mayor’s Park by the dwellers of Beşiktaş, is now closed to the public. Images of urban spaces that were once open for the enjoyment of all and which are disappearing one after the other, as shopping malls and luxury hotels are invading the best parts of the city, find a poignant expression in the book. Geçgin draws attention to the right to recreational areas and activities as a right to the city in addition to basic needs such as municipal services. The novel paints a gloomy picture of the globalising Istanbul and reads like a warning on the devastating effects of this process. Interweaving stories of migration, working-class life, periphery neighbourhoods, deindustrialisation and homelessness, Geçgin offers in this book a kaleidoscopic look at the realities of the neoliberal city through the lens of its inhabitants’ unacknowledged rights.

zh: 《人各有别》：被遗忘在“varoş”中的伊斯坦布尔
en: It Takes All Kinds: The Istanbul Forgotten in the ‘Varoş’

zh: 哈蒂杰·梅里耶姆的《İnsan Kısım Yer Damar Damar》（《人各有别》）出版于2008年，是另一部以伊斯坦布尔边缘为背景的小说，这次的时间是21世纪头十年。
它讲述了住在旧棚户区中的两姐妹的生活。书名是一句俗谚，直译是：人有多种，土有多脉。以俗谚——口头文化的一个要素——为标题，表明口头传统在主人公人生观中的重要性。标题与作品的叙事技巧结合起来，暗示人们彼此分隔、缺乏沟通，即便身处同一个家庭也是如此。
en: ) by Hatice Meryem, published in 2008, is another novel set on the periphery of Istanbul, this time in the 2000s.

It is about the lives of two sisters living in a former shanty town. The book’s title is an adage which can literally be translated as: humans have many kinds, soil has many veins. The title being an adage, an element of oral culture, signals the significance of the oral tradition in the protagonist’s outlook on life. The title, combined with the work’s narrative technique, implies the separateness and a lack of communication amongst people even within the same family.

zh: 小说中，与城市权利直接相关的主题，表现为物质需要，尤其是市政服务与基础设施。梅里耶姆通过小说的场景设置，巧妙地把生活在城市郊外旧棚户区中的孤立状态，与居民不了解自己作为城市人口一员所享有的权利，这两个主题联系起来。大量使用自由间接话语，使她能够避免以权威姿态发言，而从亲历者的眼中描写旧棚户区的生活。
在这部具有尖锐讽刺锋芒的小说中，梅里耶姆展开这些主题，却不流于鼓动；她邀请读者质疑关于所谓
街区及其居民的主导话语，却不武断地下断语。
en: In the novel, themes directly related to the right to the city appear in terms of material necessities, particularly services of the municipality and infrastructure. Meryem skilfully connects the themes of isolation on the outskirts of the city in a former shanty town and its inhabitants’ unawareness of their rights as members of the city’s population through the setting of her novel. The intensive use of free indirect discourse enables her to refrain from an authoritative attitude and depict life in a former shanty town through the eyes of those who experience it.
In her novel, which displays a sharp satirical edge, Meryem extends the themes without sliding into agitation and invites readers to question the dominant discourse on the so-called
neighbourhoods and their population without being assertive.

zh: 言说的力量与对语言的掌握，是小说的核心主题之一，一开篇便已出现：妹妹埃尔马斯被描述为与姐姐、亦即主人公祖姆鲁特截然相反的人。埃尔马斯不善言辞，令祖姆鲁特反感，因为“有一件事她［祖姆鲁特］受不了，就是不说话的人”（Meryem 2008，20）。祖姆鲁特能把言辞用作武器，而“埃尔马斯害怕言辞”（24）。
en: The power of speech and possessing language, which is a central theme of the novel, appears at the very beginning where Elmas, the younger of the two sisters, is described as the exact opposite of Zümrüt, the older sister who is the protagonist. Elmas’s incompetence in language repulses Zümrüt, since “one thing she [Zümrüt] could not stand was a person who does not speak” (Meryem 2008, 20). While Zümrüt can use words like weapons, “Elmas was scared of words” (24).

zh: 在第五章中，叙述者提到一种语言：“这是一种也许只适合用来说话的语言”（36）。她解释，说这种语言的人以许多方式运用它，并补充：“然而，［说这种语言的人］从未想过，哪怕写下一行。他们也从未想到，自己这门用处如此之多的语言，会遭人记恨”（37）。有一天，说这种语言的地方起了火。人们无法扑灭火焰，便逃往其他城市。埃尔马斯的母亲是其中之一，她拒绝谈起这件事。除了生气时用这种语言骂人，她不再使用它。
en: In the fifth chapter of the book, the narrator mentions a language: “this was such a language that perhaps it was only good for speaking” (36). She explains that its speakers utilise their language in many ways and adds: “however [speakers of that language] had never thought of writing even one line down. Neither had it ever occurred to them that a grudge would be borne against their language, which served so many purposes” (37). One day fires start in the place where this language is spoken. Unable to extinguish the flames, the speakers of the language flee to other cities. Elmas’s mother is one of them, who refuses to talk about this event. She no longer uses this language except for cursing when she is angry.

zh: 这里即便谈不上真正的矛盾，也存在含混。叙述者一方面解释，埃尔马斯从母亲那里学会了这种语言；另一方面又解释，她的母亲与这种语言断了联系：“因为她摆出一种姿态，仿佛有意把母语留在那些熊熊燃烧的东西之中，她看上去就像一个除了骄傲之外已经失去一切的民族的最后代表”（37）。显然，故事中这门未被点名的语言是库尔德语。埃尔马斯的母亲及其他村民因为火灾而被迫逃离家园，明确指向土耳其东部库尔德村庄的人口清空：在这一过程中，村庄奉官方命令遭到焚烧（Cengiz 2013）。埃尔马斯认为这种未具名的语言只能说、从未被写下，这清楚地指向过去土耳其禁止用库尔德语出版的事实。这也就是她从未读过任何以这种语言写成的东西的原因。
en: There is vagueness if not an actual contradiction, here. While the narrator explains that Elmas learned this language from her mother, she also explains that Elmas’s mother is disconnected from this language: “since she assumed a pose as if she left her mother tongue behind intentionally among all those things which burnt furiously, she looked like the final representative of a people which has lost everything apart from their pride” (37). It is obvious that this unnamed language in the story is Kurdish. Elmas’s mother and fellow villagers having to flee the place because of the fires is an explicit reference to the depopulation of Kurdish villages in Eastern Turkey, a process in which villages were set on fire by official order (Cengiz 2013). Elmas’s perception of the unnamed language as being only spoken and never written is a clear reference to the illegality of publishing in Kurdish in Turkey in the past. That is why she has never read anything in this language.

zh: 对于这门未具名的语言，有几点值得分析。埃尔马斯和祖姆鲁特是姐妹，所以说这种语言的女人是她们共同的母亲；但被同这种语言联系起来的，只有较为沉默的埃尔马斯。读者几乎会忘记，那位不得不抛下母语的母亲，也是祖姆鲁特的母亲。祖姆鲁特精通土耳其语，熟练运用各种谚语、成语和俗话。小说并没有交代，祖姆鲁特是否也像埃尔马斯一样，曾从母亲那里学过那门未具名的语言。不论学过与否，似乎都无关紧要。在伊斯坦布尔住了很久的祖姆鲁特，与土耳其语相联系。她用丰富的土耳其语说个不停。与另一种语言相联系的埃尔马斯，最近才迁来伊斯坦布尔，而且始终沉默。可以从迁移与少数族群同化之间的联系，来理解埃尔马斯的沉默。在获得城市身份的道路上，来自少数族群的迁入者首先必须抛下自己的母语。否则，她或他就会受到排斥，无法在城市中生存。梅里耶姆通过两姐妹的性格塑造，含蓄地讨论了同化与迁移的这种关联。
en: There are a couple of points worthy of analysis regarding this unnamed language. Although Elmas and Zümrüt are sisters, therefore the woman who speaks that language is the mother of both of them, it is only Elmas, the more silent of the sisters, who is identified with this language. The reader almost forgets that the mother who had to leave her native tongue behind is also Zümrüt’s mother. Zümrüt is a master of the Turkish language, with all sorts of adages, idioms and sayings. The novel does not include any information on whether Zümrüt, like Elmas, learned that unnamed language from her mother at one point. Whether she did or not, this does not seem to have any importance. Zümrüt, who has been in Istanbul for a long time, is associated with the Turkish language. She speaks endlessly in a rich Turkish. Elmas, who is associated with the other language, has recently migrated to Istanbul, and she is always silent. This silence of Elmas can be interpreted in terms of the connection between migration and the assimilation of the ethnic minority. On the way to an urban identity, the migrant from the ethnic minority has to, first of all, leave her or his native language behind. Otherwise, she or he is excluded and cannot survive in the city. Meryem implicitly addresses this correlation between assimilation and migration through the characterisations of the two sisters.

zh: 小说中，梅里耶姆从女性视角观察一个名叫科兹卢克的旧棚户区的生活。这个虚构地点是城市郊外一个孤立的街区：小巴是这类区域连接市中心的主要交通工具，却从未在书中出现。主人公祖姆鲁特有四个儿子，连他们各自哪年出生都记不清。她不满丈夫贾维特旺盛的性欲，常找借口躲避性生活。贾维特的弟弟乔什昆看待祖姆鲁特的方式，是其人物塑造中重要的一面。他不赞同她对待丈夫贾维特的态度，又因她不遮住乳沟而极为恼火。在科兹卢克，如同所有贫困的边缘街区一样，父权规范在一定程度上延续了乡村观念的僵硬。“名誉”观念与乡村语境中的相似，很容易被操纵，用来对付女性。例如，街区里的詹森——他的母亲因所谓“名誉”被她的丈夫杀害——就污蔑做家政的女性，说她们除了打扫之外还干“别的”事（145）。据祖姆鲁特说，科兹卢克的男人全都打老婆，而女人则认为自己该挨打（153）。
en: In the novel, Meryem looks at life in a former shanty town called Kozluk through a female lens. This fictional place is an isolated neighbourhood on the outskirts of the city: minibuses, a central means of transport in such areas which connects them with the city centre, never appear in the book. Zümrüt, the protagonist, has four sons whose birth years she cannot remember. She is not happy with her husband Cavit’s high libido, and much of the time tries to find excuses to avoid sex. The way Coşkun, Cavit’s brother, perceives Zümrüt is a significant aspect of her characterisation. He does not approve of the way she treats her husband Cavit and is very much annoyed because she does not cover her cleavage. In Kozluk, like all the poor periphery neighbourhoods, patriarchal norms continue the rigidity of rural perception to a certain extent. The concept of ‘honour’, akin to that in the rural context, can easily be manipulated and used against women. Cansın from the neighbourhood, whose mother was killed by her husband as a matter of ‘honour’, for instance, slanders domestic worker women for doing ‘other’ things than cleaning (145). According to Zümrüt, the men of Kozluk all beat their wives and the women think they deserve it (153).

zh: 消费主义与城市身份之间的关系，是《人各有别》的核心主题。科兹卢克的购物中心——科兹卢克中心——在小说的视觉意象中占据主导地位，是这种关系的主要象征。这一意象也指向购物中心为科兹卢克这样的旧棚户区等贫困区域所赋予的人造城市外观。书中几次隐约提及一个与这座购物中心有关的秘密，埃尔马斯也牵涉其中（100、237）。这也许不是卖淫，而可能是某种以调情换取物质利益的活动。购物中心是消费主义最鲜明的象征，因此，这种近似卖淫的活动以科兹卢克中心为场所，值得注意。
en: The correlation between consumerism and urban identity is a central theme in

. Kozluk Centre, the shopping mall of Kozluk, which dominates the visual imagery in the novel, is the main symbol of this correlation. In this imagery there is also a reference to the artificial urban look that shopping malls give to poor areas such as former shanty towns like Kozluk. In several instances, there is an implicit reference to a secret connected with this shopping mall, in which Elmas is also involved (100, 237). This is perhaps not prostitution, but might be some sort of flirtation in exchange for material benefit. Since shopping malls are the ultimate symbol of consumerism, the setting of this prostitution-like activity at the Kozluk Centre is worthy of note.

zh: 通过消费获得城市性

与科兹卢克旧棚户区毗邻的，是城市中产阶级的封闭式社区。科兹卢克的女人去那里做清洁工，因而见识到其中的生活。早在20世纪80年代初，坦瑟·申亚珀勒便如此描述棚户区女性与其服务的城市中产阶级女雇主的相遇：“［她们］进入中产阶级家庭，近距离观察中产阶级生活”；这“激发了新的渴求、希望和向往，却未能得到满足，因而使gecekondu［棚户区］女性更加不快乐”（1981，208）。梅里耶姆描绘了21世纪头十年伊斯坦布尔的类似处境，此时贫富鸿沟已大为加深；她以强烈的空间维度处理阶级问题。
en: Side by side with the former shanty town of Kozluk are the gated communities of the urban middle class. The women of Kozluk witness the lives in them when they go there as cleaners. Back in the beginning of the 1980s, Tansı Şenyapılı describes the encounter between shanty town women and urban middle-class women, whose houses they clean, as follows: “[they] entered middle class houses and observed middle class living closely” and this “stimulated new cravings, hopes and aspirations which remained unsatisfied thus causing further unhappiness among gecekondu [shanty] women” (1981, 208). Meryem depicts a similar situation in the Istanbul of the 2000s, where the divide between the wealthy and the poor is much deeper, addressing the issue of class with a strong spatial dimension.

zh: 如第3章详细讨论的，对于迁入女性而言，城市消费模式意味着城市化。“对于迁入家庭，‘像城市人那样消费’是成为城市人的首要条件，而这一点由女性来安排”（Kıray 1999，174）。在这样做时，女性将满足家庭基本需要的消费压到最低，却对能让别人看见的商品实行“炫耀性消费”（174）。克赖补充，“流动商贩与分期付款销售”使之成为可能（174）。坦瑟·申亚珀勒也指出，“电视和浅易读物渗入社会交往匮乏的棚户区环境，有效地灌输一套以消费为导向的价值体系，导致女性产生不必要的渴求、无法满足的欲望、对自身阶级的疏离，以及随之而来的不快乐”（1981，207）。小说家通过主人公祖姆鲁特的形象，以现实主义方式处理了这些欲望。
en: As discussed in detail in Chapter 3, for migrant women, urban consumption patterns signify urbanisation. “For the migrant family ‘consuming like urbanites’ is the first condition of being an urbanite and women organise this” (Kıray 1999, 174). While doing that, women keep their consumption for basic family needs at minimum, but for goods that will be seen by others they implement “conspicuous consumption” (174). Kıray adds that “itinerant merchants and instalment selling” make this possible (174). As Tansı Şenyapılı observes “T.V. and simple reading material which penetrate the socially hungry gecekondu environment, effectively impose a consumption oriented value system which leads to needless cravings, unsatisfied desires, alienation from one’s own class, and consequent unhappiness among women” (1981, 207). The novelist realistically addresses such desires through the portrayal of Zümrüt, the protagonist.

zh: 在为小说撰写的导言中，梅里耶姆说，许多科兹卢克女性追随一种“时尚”，去科兹卢克“每条街上如雨后春笋般冒出来的”私人医院生孩子（9）。这一描述也暗示了小说的时代背景，即21世纪头十年。记述科兹卢克发展过程的那一章结尾交代：埃尔马斯搬来科兹卢克的那一年，街区女人们给窗户挂上了凸花花边窗帘，认识了电视上的女性节目，有些人甚至去演播室当这些节目的现场观众，并且习惯了使用手机（34）。小说用整整一章写博尔贾姆——一种可以放进烤箱的玻璃器皿，祖姆鲁特把它视为精美的厨具（78）。她认为这是非常珍贵的东西，兴奋地盼望自己拥有它的那一天。最后，她在当地街市分期付款买了一个。当她把博尔贾姆捧在手里时，书中把她描写为“变成了一个完全不同的女人，一个住在离科兹卢克很远的地方的女人”（80）。不幸的是，这个炫耀性消费的故事悲伤收场：过了一阵，埃尔马斯不慎把它打碎了。
en: In the introduction she writes to her novel, Meryem states that a high number of Kozlukite women have been following “the fashion” of giving birth in private hospitals “which have been mushrooming on every street” in Kozluk (9). This description also alludes to the period in which the novel is set, which is the 2000s. The chapter which chronicles the development of Kozluk ends with the information that the year Elmas moved to Kozluk was also the year when the women of the neighbourhood put guipure lace curtains on their windows, became acquainted with women’s programmes on television, some of them even went to television studios as audience members on these programmes, and got used to using mobile phones (34). There is an entire chapter on Borcam, a glassware dish that can be put in the oven, which Zümrüt regards as a fancy piece of kitchenware (78). She regards it as a highly precious item and excitedly awaits the day she will possess it. She eventually purchases one, to be paid in instalments, from the local street market. As she holds her Borcam in her hands, she is depicted as having “changed into an entirely different woman, one who lives very far from Kozluk” (80). Unfortunately, this story of conspicuous consumption ends sadly since the Borcam is accidently broken by Elmas after a while.

zh: 通过消费实现城市化的努力，与消费主义在当今世界达到的深广程度，相互放大了彼此的效果。这两种现象的交织在小说中多次出现。例如，科兹卢克人把棚屋换成公寓楼时，虽然连楼梯扶手、炉子烟管等建筑的基本设施都负担不起，却使用复合木地板、丝光涂料和PVC窗框（70）。在极富幽默感的“另一种生活的梦想藏在客厅里”一章中（94），这两个主题交汇。祖姆鲁特公寓的客厅，只有客人来访时才开门。房间里塞满她买下、保存却从未使用的东西：多莱斯茶杯、电动咖啡研磨机、吸尘器、仿银茶碟、套几、塑料花，等等。祖姆鲁特一进入这个房间，连走路和坐下的姿态都变了（95）。叙述者幽默地说，这个房间“变成了一家日用品商店的仓库”（95）。按祖姆鲁特的说法，房间里的东西是给配得上的人用的，而她家里人没有一个配得上（95）。小说的这一描写，直接表现了克赖所说迁入者家中“一屋屋从未使用的东西”（1999，174）。
en: The effort towards urbanisation through consumption and the great extent to which consumerism has reached in today’s world both multiply each other’s effects. The intertwinement of the two phenomena is present in various instances in the novel. For instance, Kozlukites use laminated flooring, satin paint and PVC window frames when they are replacing their shanties with apartment buildings, although they cannot afford the basic needs of buildings, such as banisters and stove pipes (70). The two themes merge in a highly humorous chapter entitled “Another Life’s Dream Is Hidden in Guest Rooms” (94). In Zümrüt’s flat, the door of the guest room is only opened when they have visitors. The room is full of goods bought and kept by Zümrüt but never used: Duralex tea cups, an electric coffee grinder, a hoover, fake silver saucers, nesting tables, plastic flowers and so forth. When Zümrüt enters this room, even the way she walks and sits changes (95). The narrator humorously describes the room as “having transformed into the depot of a store which sells household goods” (95). According to Zümrüt, the goods in the room are for those who are worth it and none of her family members are (95). This depiction in the novel is a direct expression of what Kıray describes as “roomfuls of unused goods” in migrants’ houses (1999, 174).
