zh: 与姐姐祖姆鲁特一样，埃尔马斯也梦想着中产阶级生活。一天，她在回家路上的街边捡到几本书：一本英语书、一本烹饪书，以及一本讲做母亲和养育孩子的书。这些被封闭式社区某位居民扔掉的书，让埃尔马斯得以一窥城市中产阶级的生活：它近在步行可及之处，却又远如另一个星球。埃尔马斯把烹饪书带回家，读遍所有食谱，幻想打开封面图片上的橱柜，取出自己从未听过名字的食材，在那些闪亮的锅里烹调。下一章中，她把书带进厨房。当她和祖姆鲁特开始为晚间野餐做葡萄叶包饭时，祖姆鲁特决定听埃尔马斯念书里的食谱，尽管她其实知道做法。然而，这份用到橄榄油和其他昂贵食材的食谱惹恼了她，埃尔马斯后悔没有预料到这一点。埃尔马斯望着书，开始幻想“那美好的一天”（44）。她不知道那一天自己将做什么、穿什么、吃什么，却知道自己会非常快乐。她也提醒自己，那一天之后，她绝不会再去科兹卢克中心。
en: Like her sister Zümrüt, Elmas has dreams about a middle-class life. One day she finds a couple of books in the street on her way home: an English book, a cookery book, and a book about motherhood and raising children. These books thrown away by someone living in the gated communities offer Elmas a few glimpses of the urban middle-class life which is in walking distance yet as remote as another planet. Elmas takes the cookery book home. She reads all the recipes in it and fantasises about opening the cupboards in the picture on the cover of the book, taking ingredients whose names she has never heard of before and cooking them in those bright cooking pans. In the next chapter, she brings the book to the kitchen. As she and Zümrüt start stuffing the vine leaves for the evening picnic, Zümrüt decides to hear Elmas read out the recipe in the book, although she actually knows how to cook it. However, this recipe, with olive oil and some other expensive ingredients in it, annoys her, and Elmas regrets not anticipating this. Looking at the book, Elmas starts daydreaming about “that beautiful day” (44). She has no idea as to what she will do, wear or eat on that day, but she knows that she will be very happy. She also reminds herself that she will never go to the Kozluk Centre after that day.

zh: 小说中，科兹卢克中心大约建成于埃尔马斯搬进街区之时。科兹卢克的女人喜欢在里面闲逛，即便买不起其中的东西。乔什昆和朋友们也到这里扒窃。他们的一个朋友认为，这正是下手的好地方，因为没钱的人也成了“购物狂”（178）。叙述者把他们描写成这样一群人：“凭口袋里的信用卡，欠下比自己身体还大的债”，而且“除了钱和漂亮的新东西，什么都不想碰”（178）。科兹卢克中心作为消费主义最鲜明的象征出现，而小说对消费主义进行了尖锐批评。
en: In the novel, the Kozluk Centre was built around the time Elmas moved into the neighbourhood. The women of Kozluk like strolling through it, even if they cannot shop there. This is where Coşkun and his friends go pickpocketing. According to a friend of theirs, it is the right place to do that because people without money have become “shopping maniacs” (178). The narrator describes them as “this crowd who would get into debt bigger than their bodies, with the credit cards in their pockets” who “want to touch nothing but money and fancy new stuff” (178). The Kozluk Centre appears as the ultimate symbol of consumerism, which is sharply criticised in the novel.

zh: 科兹卢克迁入女性对城市中产阶级生活的仰慕，与安纳托利亚女性对肥皂剧所描绘生活的迷恋并不相同。科兹卢克的女人并非在电视上看到这种生活，而是就住在它旁边。因此，她们的处境远不止简单的仰慕：这是一个以空间要素为核心的身份问题。祖姆鲁特捧着博尔贾姆——她炫耀性消费的物件——时，看上去像个“住在离科兹卢克很远的地方”的女人（80）。对于生活在棚户区或旧棚户区的迁入女性，向往更高阶级的生活，不仅源于对奢华生活的欲望，也源于对城市身份的追寻，因为那些较富裕群体中的女性，是她们获得这种身份的唯一榜样。她们不熟悉那些具有城市身份、却与她们社会经济地位相近的女性，例如无产阶级中的进步成员，或在不同部门、不同层级工作、积极参与工会或其他进步事业的女性。没有这样的榜样时，成为城市女性，就等同于成为城市中产阶级女性，因为棚户区女性对城市女性的认识，仅限于这一类别中的例子。梅里耶姆以现实主义方式处理了这一困境，并巧妙地描写了祖姆鲁特和埃尔马斯由此产生的消费主义向往。
en: Kozlukite migrant women’s admiration for urban middle-class life is different from Anatolian women’s fascination with the lives depicted in the soap operas they view. The women of Kozluk do not see this life on television, but live side by side with it. Consequently, their situation is much more than simple admiration: it is an issue of identity, with the spatial element at its core: Zümrüt looks like a woman “who lives very far from Kozluk” as she carries the Borcam (80), the item of her conspicuous consumption. For migrant women living in shanty towns or former shanty towns, the aspiration to a life of the higher classes not only derives from their desire for a life of luxury, but also from a search for an urban identity, since their only role models for this identity are women from these wealthier groups. They are not familiar with women who are urban yet close to them in terms of socioeconomic strata, such as progressive members of the proletariat or women working in different sectors and levels who are active in unions or other progressive causes. When no such role model exists for them, being an urban woman becomes equated with being an urban middle-class woman since the shanty town women’s perception of the urban woman is limited to the examples of this category. Meryem realistically addresses this dilemma and skilfully depicts the consequent consumerist aspirations of Zümrüt and Elmas.

zh: 辨识科兹卢克
书中没有明确指明科兹卢克的位置。不过，这一虚构场景似乎受到阿尔纳武特柯伊区一些街区的启发，因为同属这个区的真实街区哈德姆柯伊出现在小说中（164）。对巴克尔柯伊（184）和耶尼卡帕（202）的提及，也支持这一可能性。让-弗朗索瓦·佩鲁兹将阿尔纳武特柯伊描述为位于伊斯坦布尔“断裂的边缘地带”的一个区（2018，34）。
en: The book does not include any explicit references to the location of Kozluk. However, this fictional setting seems to be inspired by neighbourhoods in the district of Arnavutköy, since the factual neighbourhood of Hadımköy, which is also in this district, appears in the novel (164). The mention of Bakırköy (184) and Yenikapı (202) supports this probability. Jean-François Pérouse describes Arnavutköy as a district on Istanbul’s “riven fringe belt” (2018, 34).

zh: 第一部第十三章集中呈现祖姆鲁特对科兹卢克的看法；但在此前的一章，她已这样评论自己的街区：“整个科兹卢克，凡是住在科兹卢克的人，都是废物。［……］就算整个科兹卢克飞走了，也没人会察觉”（50）。在后面那一章，她的观察范围广得多。这里，埃尔马斯转述祖姆鲁特对科兹卢克的议论：“用姐姐绘声绘色的说法，这是懒汉和闲人、穷光蛋和倒霉鬼、贫嘴和小偷、落魄汉、坏种、无赖和光腿穷人落脚的地方”（67）。埃尔马斯接着说，在祖姆鲁特看来，“长着男人般面孔的科兹卢克女人”（67），操心晚上做什么吃的，把压力发泄到丈夫和孩子身上。她认为，科兹卢克的男人可分为“有工作的和没工作的”（67），而街区里后者很多。科兹卢克的女人把丈夫看成“没长成的男人”（68）。孩子们没有保暖衣服，冬天受冻；夏天却过得很快活，卖水、纸巾和公交车票赚些钱，一直玩到深夜。对年轻人，祖姆鲁特的评价很负面：“他们几乎没有一个会走上正路，不是成小偷，就是成坏蛋”（69）。她把科兹卢克早年住棚屋的日子与今天作比较。虽然过去常停水停电，道路没有铺沥青，每场暴雨过后街上都泥泞不堪，如今许多女人却怀念起自己从前看不起的棚屋。至少那时能养几只鸡，能在门前种些菜。而且，现在科兹卢克所有空地都成了废品堆场（70）。对棚屋尚未被公寓楼取代时的旧科兹卢克的怀念，是祖姆鲁特心中的核心情绪。后来她去拜访新邻居时，向他们讲述街区往事，怀念那个虽常停水停电、却绿意盎然、有鸡有羊的科兹卢克（103）。通过祖姆鲁特的这些评论，小说对棚户住房的积极态度变得清楚，涉及支持棚户住房论点的两个核心方面：第一，在缺乏福利住房政策的情况下，棚屋作为栖身之所具有必然性；第二，它与自然相和谐。这里再一次通过人物的评论传递信息，而非借助以权威口吻发言的叙述者。
en: The thirteenth chapter of Part I focuses on Zümrüt’s views on Kozluk, but before that, in an earlier chapter, she makes the following comment on her neighbourhood: “all Kozluk and whoever lives in Kozluk were wastrels. [...] if the whole of Kozluk flew away, nobody would feel it” (50). Her observations in the later chapter are much wider in scope. Here, Elmas reports Zümrüt’s speech on Kozluk: “with her sister’s colourful description, this was a place where layabouts and loafers, stony-brokes and hoodoos, sauceboxes and thieves, down-and-outs, bad lots, hangdogs and the barelegged settle down” (67). Elmas continues by saying that according to Zümrüt, “the women of Kozluk with their mannish faces” (67) are concerned about what to cook for the evening and deflect their stress onto their husbands and children. For her, the men of Kozluk can be divided into “those with a job and those without” (67), and there is a considerable number of the latter in the neighbourhood. The women of Kozluk regard their husbands as “half-formed men” (68). The children are without any warm clothes and suffer from the cold in the winter, but they have a great time in the summer making some money by selling water, tissue paper and bus tickets, and playing until late at night. On the youngsters, Zümrüt speaks negatively: “almost none of them would mend their ways, they would become either thieves or rascals” (69). She compares the early days of Kozluk, when they lived in shanties, with today. Although they used to have water and electricity cuts, and after every rainstorm the streets would be muddy as they had no asphalt on the roads, today many women long for their shanties, which they looked down on in the past. At least they had some chickens and they could grow some vegetables in front of their homes. Besides, all of the open pieces of land in Kozluk have now been turned into junkyards (70). Nostalgia for old Kozluk, before the shanties were replaced with apartment buildings, is a central feeling in Zümrüt’s psyche. In a later example, when she goes to visit her new neighbours, she tells them stories about the neighbourhood’s past, longing for the green Kozluk with animals such as chickens and sheep, despite the frequent electricity and water cuts (103). The positive approach to shanty housing in the novel becomes clear through these comments by Zümrüt, in terms of two central tenets of the pro-shanty argument: first, inevitability of the shanty as shelter in the absence of welfare housing policies; second, its harmony with nature. Once again, the message is conveyed through the comments of the characters rather than through a narrator speaking with authority.

zh: 在整部小说中，梅里耶姆运用对话、自由间接话语和心理叙述，呈现人物对科兹卢克的感受。临近结尾，乔什昆碰到有阵子没露面的朋友萨米。他们聊起来，萨米说“该死的科兹卢克”，又“痛苦地”说，“再也不会踏进这里一步”（264）。谈话结束时，萨米告诉乔什昆：“你也快逃出这地狱吧！”（265）。萨米害怕打算报复他的詹森，所以这样说；但这些话也表现了他对自己街区的感受。同样，对埃尔马斯而言，科兹卢克是一个将她困住的可怕地方：“她［……］明白了，科兹卢克这个地狱，没有一扇门通向‘美好的一天’”（270）。在詹森同戏剧圈来往的情节中，几次提及贝伊奥卢——伊斯坦布尔文化、艺术以及夜生活的中心。它在乔什昆、詹森与萨米的谈话中出现，是一个遥远的地方，一个与他们所处世界截然不同的世界。
en: Meryem uses dialogues, free indirect discourse and psycho-narration to introduce the characters’ feelings about Kozluk throughout the novel. Towards the end of the book, Coşkun comes across his friend Sami, who has not been around for a while. When they start chatting, Sami says “Goddamn Kozluk” and “in agony” he says that “he will never set foot here again” (264). At the end of their chat, Sami tells Coşkun: “you too, run away from this hell!” (265). Sami’s fear of Cansın, who plans revenge, makes him talk this way, but his words also manifest his feelings about his neighbourhood. Similarly, for Elmas, Kozluk is a terrible place she is stuck in: “she [...] understood that there was no door opening to a ‘beautiful day’ from the Kozluk hell” (270). Within the scope of Cansın’s relations with theatre circles, there are a couple of references to Beyoğlu, the centre of Istanbul’s culture and arts as well as nightlife. It enters the conversations of Coşkun, Cansın and Sami as a remote place, a world completely distinct from where they live.

zh: 乔什昆在狱中变成了一个很不一样的人，他想向所有人证明自己已经改变，想成为科兹卢克孩子们的榜样：“有时他甚至想，自己会成为榜样，成为那些同种种不可能抗争的科兹卢克孩子的纪元起点”（112）。在这集中呈现他内心世界的一章中，我们听到关于他对科兹卢克看法的心理叙述。对他来说，科兹卢克是个“懦夫聚集的地方”；这些人从不互相信任，什么都怕：“怕隔壁邻居、自己的母亲、父亲、自己的孩子，怕同自己挽着胳膊走路的最好朋友［……］，怕治安力量，怕市政当局［……］，谁都怕”（116—117）。乔什昆的这些想法呼应书名，突出科兹卢克人彼此隔绝。这是《人各有别》思想表达的重要一点，使它有别于许多以更早年代为背景、能感受到世界主义团结的街区小说。《人各有别》如书名所暗示的，特别强调这种世界主义团结的缺失。
en: When Coşkun becomes a very different person whilst in prison, he wants to show everyone that he has changed, and wants to become a role model for the children of Kozluk: “there were even times when he thought that he would be a role model, a year zero for Kozlukite children struggling against impossibilities” (112). In the same chapter, which focuses on his inner world, we hear the psycho-narration of his thoughts on Kozluk. For him Kozluk is “a place of cowards” who never trust each other and who are scared of everything: “would be scared of their next-door neighbour, their mother, their father, their own child, their best friend, with whom they walk arm in arm [...] the forces of security, the municipality [...] scared of one and all” (116–117). Echoing the title of the book, these thoughts of Coşkun accentuate the separateness of Kozlukites. This is an important point about
’s messages which separates it from numerous neighbourhood novels set in earlier decades where a sense of cosmopolitan solidarity can be felt. In
, as implied in its title, there is particular emphasis on the lack of such cosmopolitan solidarity.

zh: 关于科兹卢克的另一段文字由叙述者的评论构成，呈现出外部视角。住在城市中心地区的人，会以带有贬义的
来形容科兹卢克这类地方。佩琳·坦在讨论
概念时强调：“盗窃、谋杀、卖淫、毒品、激进左翼倾向和恐怖活动，是国家与媒体用来将
刑事化的话语代码”（2008，410）。伊斯兰主义原教旨主义也可能列入这份话语代码清单。如下面将讨论的，叙述者的方式有别于把科兹卢克这样的街区当作
、使之他者化的主导话语。在分析这一点之前，先看一看导言会有帮助。
en: Another passage on Kozluk comprises the narrator’s comments which appear as a viewpoint from outside. Kozluk is a place which would in a pejorative manner be described as a
by those living in the central areas of the city. Writing about the concept of

, Pelin Tan stresses that “theft, murder, prostitution, drugs, radical leftist tendencies and terror are the discursive codes the state and the media use to criminalize the varoşes” (2008, 410). Islamist fundamentalism might also appear in this list of discursive codes. As discussed below, the narrator’s approach is different from the dominant discourse otherising neighbourhoods like Kozluk as
. Before analysing this, it would be useful to have a look at the introduction.

zh: 在小说导言中，梅里耶姆把科兹卢克描述为“稍稍越过［伊斯坦布尔］，又稍稍在它前面，稍稍偏右，又稍稍偏左——但无论如何都不在中心”（9）；她把科兹卢克的居民称作科兹卢克人。这一称呼似乎并不暗示街区身份——例如《重罗曼》中科莱拉人的身份——而是在表明科兹卢克居民在城市中的局外人地位：科兹卢克人与中心地区居民形成对照，后者被她称作伊斯坦布尔人。当“科兹卢克的孩子”在博斯普鲁斯海峡游泳时，“乘坐市内渡轮、过着娇贵生活的伊斯坦布尔人”（10）对他们作出负面反应。
en: In the introduction to her novel Meryem describes Kozluk as “a little past [Istanbul], a little before it, a little to the right of it and a little to the left – but by no means in the centre” (9); and she refers to the dwellers of Kozluk as Kozlukites. Rather than an implication of the neighbourhood identity as, for instance, that of Kolerites in

, here this description seems to indicate the Kozluk inhabitants’ outsider position in the city, a contrast between Kozlukites versus those living in the central areas, whom she describes as Istanbulites: when “Kozlukite children” swim in the Bosporus, “Istanbulites who travel on intra-city ferries and live tender lives” (10) react negatively towards them.

zh: 这篇充满苦甜交织的幽默的导言，以观察科兹卢克女性的潮流开篇，例如在私人医院生孩子。话题由此转向科兹卢克的婴儿和儿童；作者告诉我们，科兹卢克的孩子如何毫不犹豫地到受污染的溪流、水渠和博斯普鲁斯海峡等不适宜的地方游泳。作者解释，科兹卢克的母亲在孩子空闲时送他们去学《古兰经》或缝纫；孩子们梦想的，却是“柔道和跆拳道课程，以及大型购物中心闪亮的橱窗”（10）。这一观察表明，在科兹卢克，对中产阶级城市性的向往及其消费主义欲望，从童年就开始了。
en: The introduction which is full of bitter-sweet humour starts with observations on trends among Kozlukite women, such as giving birth in private hospitals. The subject moves from here to the babies and children in Kozluk and the author tells us about how Kozlukite children do not hesitate to swim in inappropriate places such as polluted streams, channels and the Bosporus. The author explains that Kozlukite mothers send their children to learn the Koran or how to sew in their free time; however, children dream of “judo and taekwondo courses and the glossy windows of large shopping malls” (10), an observation indicating that aspirations to middle-class urbanity with consumerist desires start at childhood in Kozluk.

zh: 作者继续说，科兹卢克的孩子很小就开始工作，无法上学，并补充，其中有些走向犯罪，有些则成为警察和军人。如前所述，在公众观念中，所谓

街区通常与犯罪联系在一起。它们当然不是犯罪中心，但确实可能找到与犯罪有关的人；考虑到这些地方的悲观氛围及改善生活机会的匮乏，这并不令人意外。梅尔文·西曼的“异化的第三种变体”（1959，787），为这类情况提供了有益解释。西曼说，这类异化“源自涂尔干对‘失范’的描述，指一种规范缺失的状态”（787）；在这种状态下，个人倾向于认为“要实现既定目标，就必须采取社会不认可的行为”（788）。如第3章所讨论的，社会学研究证明，伊斯坦布尔棚户区中并未出现异化和失范（Kıray 1982，173—174）。棚户居民对未来和向上流动抱有希望。然而，在21世纪头十年——即收入极度不平等的时代——伊斯坦布尔的旧棚户区中，城市贫困却是严峻现实，失业率高，在职贫困也存在。世界主义的团结本可为棚户区居民提供对街区及城市的依恋感；它的缺失，使这幅图景更加阴暗。梅里耶姆通过强调科兹卢克潜在的失范，现实地处理了这些事实。因此，一些读者可能认为，她在导言中谈到科兹卢克男人的犯罪倾向，或孩子不愿读书，是在再生产歧视性的
话语。然而，如果完整考察导言，并结合小说的总体立场来理解，其含义就清楚了：科兹卢克虽有一些失范情形，即有人涉入犯罪，但无论如何，这都只是街区中
的现实。
en: The author continues by stating that the children of Kozluk start working at a very young age and cannot go to school, and adds that some of these children turn to crime while some become policemen and soldiers. As mentioned above, in the public perception, so-called

neighbourhoods are usually associated with crime. Although certainly not hubs of crime, it is possible to find people connected with crime in these places which is not surprising given the pessimism and scarcity of opportunities for a better life in them. Melvin Seeman’s “third variant of alienation” (1959, 787) offers a useful explanation for such cases. Seeman states that this type of alienation is “derived from Durkheim’s description of ‘anomie,’ and refers to a condition of normlessness” (787) where the individual would incline to think “that socially unapproved behaviors are required to achieve given goals” (788). As discussed earlier in Chapter 3, sociological research proves that in the shanty towns of Istanbul alienation and anomie did not emerge (Kıray 1982, 173–174). Shanty dwellers were hopeful about their future and upward mobility. However, in the former shanty towns of Istanbul of the 2000s (i.e., times of extreme income inequality) urban poverty was a grim reality with high unemployment rates as well as in-work poverty. The absence of cosmopolitan solidarity which could offer the dwellers of shanty towns a feeling of attachment to their neighbourhood and the city makes this picture darker. Meryem addresses these facts realistically with the emphasis she puts on the potential anomie in Kozluk. Consequently, some readers might regard her comments in the introduction on Kozlukite men’s tendency to crime, or on Kozlukite children’s disinclination to study, as reproducing the discriminatory

discourse. Yet, when we evaluate the introduction in its entirety and interpret it together with the overall position of the novel, the message becomes clear: although there are some cases of anomie (i.e., people involved with crime) in Kozluk, this is, by all means, the reality
in this neighbourhood.

zh: 科兹卢克人大多数只是难以维持生计的穷人。导言以同情而幽默的方式讲述，他们很年轻便结婚、生子、抱孙子，随后就觉得人生不过如此。导言中引人注意的，是它强调，他们的生活方式是一场求生的斗争。导言并不以激起怜悯的方式描绘科兹卢克人。相反，幽默的运用使人们注意到，他们虽历经苦难，却仍有生存下去的能力。如下面将讨论的，小说的结尾尤其清楚地体现了这一点。
en: The majority of Kozlukites are simply the poor finding it hard to make ends meet. As told in a sympathetic and humorous manner in the introduction, they get married, have children and grandchildren at a very young age, and then simply feel that this is all there is in life. What is noticeable in the introduction is the accent on their way of life as a struggle for survival. The introduction does not portray Kozlukites in a way to motivate pity for them. On the contrary, the use of humour calls attention to their ability to survive, despite all the hardship they suffer from. This message of the novel is particularly visible in its ending, as discussed below.

zh: 叙述者对主人公、其他主要人物以及科兹卢克人总体上都抱有同情。在题为“科兹卢克在哪里，埃尔马斯是谁？”的一章中，叙述者的存在感最强；这一章解释乡村迁入者如何建立街区，其中一段讲述科兹卢克的历史，以现实主义细节反映棚户区之间的相似性。如同导言，这里梅里耶姆所描绘的图景，并未把科兹卢克人表现为需要怜悯的人，也未把科兹卢克表现为令人沮丧的地方。相反，在这段幽默文字中，她将科兹卢克描写为极具活力的街区。科兹卢克最初几年开办的店铺，是很好的例子。叙述者一口气列出商店名称，仿佛重现它们在短时间内接连开张的情景。她列举种类繁多的商店，把这些商店带给街区的氛围也带入描写。从中可以推知，当地居民具有一定收入和生活水准，因为那还是信用卡尚未广泛普及的时期。简单说，叙述者对科兹卢克的看法，比上一节描述的科兹卢克人自己的看法积极得多。这些描写中的活力与能量，与亨利·列斐伏尔的评论相契合：“工人阶级街区具有一种‘活泼劲儿’，让它们富有趣味，也让我们希望在别处同样找到这种活力”（2003，157）。叙述者还强调，街区的物质条件与基础设施一直在随时间改善。这一章的某些部分再次出现犯罪话题，暗示当地住着一些罪犯，或者科兹卢克的生活可能导致犯罪倾向。然而，小说再一次明确表明，大多数科兹卢克人都与犯罪或粗暴行径无关。
en: The narrator has a sympathetic approach to the protagonist and other major characters, as well as to Kozlukites in general. The narrator’s presence is at its strongest in the chapter entitled “Where Is Kozluk, Who Is Elmas?”, where the neighbourhood’s foundation by rural migrants is explained. The chapter includes a passage on the history of Kozluk, comprising realistic details that reflect the similarity of shanty towns with each other. Similar to the introduction, the picture Meryem paints here does not show Kozlukites as people to pity and Kozluk as a depressing place. On the contrary, in this humorous passage she depicts Kozluk as a highly dynamic neighbourhood. The shops that were opened in the first years of Kozluk is a good example. The narrator lists the names of the shops in one breath, in a manner reflecting the way they were opened one after the other within a short time. Listing their wide range, she carries the atmosphere these shops bring to the neighbourhood into the depiction. It is possible to infer from the passage that the dwellers of the place have a certain income and standard of living, since this is before credit cards were widely available. Put simply, the narrator’s perspective on Kozluk is much more positive than that of Kozlukites described in the above section. The dynamism and energy of Kozluk in these descriptions are in line with Henri Lefebvre’s comment that “working-class neighbourhoods have a ‘liveliness’ that makes them interesting and which we would like to find elsewhere” (2003, 157). The narrator also emphasises that physical conditions and infrastructure in the neighbourhood have been improving throughout time. In some parts of the chapter, the reappearance of the crime topic carries the implication that some criminals live in the place, or that life in Kozluk may result in a disposition to crime. However, again, the novel’s message that the majority of Kozlukites do not have anything to do with crime or rough ways is explicit.

zh: 科兹卢克的基础设施和环境问题，使这个旧棚户区的生活更加艰难。梅里耶姆主要通过这些问题展开小说的城市权利主题。书中一处，叙述者如此讽刺人们对科兹卢克这类区域的普遍看法：“那些把生在这座城市视为倒霉的现代城市规划者，不断组织一个又一个论坛，反复讨论这些一半像棚屋、一半像公寓楼的建筑如何破坏城市轮廓”（33）。这里讽刺的对象，是专家们只顾这些街区难看的外观，却不关心其严重的基础设施和环境问题，以及居民的权利与需要。
en: The infrastructural and environmental issues in Kozluk deepens the difficulty of life in this former shanty town. Meryem develops the theme of the right to the city in her novel primarily through these problems. At one point in the book, the narrator satirises the widespread perception of areas like Kozluk as follows: “modern urban planners who regard having been born in this city as bad luck keep organising forum after forum, discuss over and over again that these structures, which partly look like a shanty and partly like an apartment building, destroy the silhouette of the city” (33). The object of sarcasm here is the experts’ preoccupation with the unsightly appearance of these neighbourhoods instead of their severe infrastructural and environmental problems, and the rights and needs of their inhabitants.

zh: 通过自由间接话语或人物对话引入这些问题，梅里耶姆得以立足人物经验，从人物立场处理城市权利问题；换言之，是从饱受这些问题之苦的人眼中来处理。有一处，祖姆鲁特把科兹卢克的两大根本问题概括为“废品堆场和臭屎沟”（36）。人们把金属废品扔到科兹卢克的一处空地，居民阻止这种行为的尝试毫无成效。他们向市政当局申请，甚至上电视节目反映，却都没有结果。同样，一条混着污水的溪流也是科兹卢克长期以来的问题。随着小说展开，我们得知，市长候选人曾来到科兹卢克，祖姆鲁特当面向他抱怨此事。提起这次相遇，她解释，市长忙着美化富人的街道，根本没时间管这个问题（63）。她补充，这条溪流里流的是附近昂贵封闭式社区的污水（63）。她指望其他科兹卢克人赞赏自己的反抗。然而，他们害怕这个人一旦当选市长，会断掉他们的供水。因此，他们感到担忧，并不赞赏祖姆鲁特勇敢的举动。这一担忧是关键细节，突出科兹卢克人如何理解自己在城市中的存在：他们把最基本的市政服务也看作恩惠，而不是权利。毫不奇怪，在恩惠的另一面，他们看到的是惩罚；哪怕稍稍抱怨，他们也料想会招致惩罚。
en: Introducing these problems through free indirect discourse, or dialogues of characters, Meryem manages to address the issues of the right to the city from the standpoint of the characters via their experiences; in other words, through the eyes of those who suffer from these problems. In one instance, Zümrüt summarises the two fundamental issues of Kozluk as “the junkyard and the shitty stream” (36). People throw metal junk into an empty site in Kozluk, and Kozlukites’ attempts to stop this fail to yield any results. They apply to the municipal authorities; they even talk on television programmes; but they cannot get results. Similarly, a stream mixed with sewage water is a long-standing problem in Kozluk. As the novel proceeds, it comes out that, at one point, when the candidate for municipal mayor is in Kozluk, Zümrüt complains to him about this. Referring to this encounter, she explains that the mayor does not have time for the problem since he is too busy making rich people’s streets look nicer (63). She adds that this stream carries the sewage water of the expensive gated communities nearby (63). She expects fellow Kozlukites to appreciate her rebellious behaviour. However, they fear that if this man becomes mayor, he will cut off their water. Therefore, they are worried and do not appreciate Zümrüt’s courageous behaviour. Such a worry is a crucial detail stressing the Kozlukites’ perception about their existence in the city: they consider even the most basic municipal services as a favour rather than a right. Unsurprisingly, on the other side of the favour they see punishment, which they expect as a result of even a minor complaint.

zh: 小说城市权利主题的另一维度，是休闲场所的可及性。小说以一次家庭野餐的准备和进行开篇。活动时间临近，祖姆鲁特担心他们抢不到海边公园前部的位置。叙述者详细解释，这座公园给科兹卢克女性的生活带来了多大改变：白天，她们喜欢带女儿去那里野餐（209）；晚上，则同丈夫一起去。在公共绿地稀少的伊斯坦布尔，公园全满时，有些城市居民甚至在路边小块绿地上野餐。在“不合适的地方”野餐，让精英主义者感到厌恶，他们认为这与城市礼仪相违背。他们不批评城市绿地的不可及，却攻击野餐者，说他们不懂城市文明。梅里耶姆从人物视角呈现对绿地的需要，把它表现为享有休闲场所的权利问题。
en: The other dimension of the right to the city theme in the novel comprises access to recreational areas. The novel starts with the preparations for and the experiencing of a family picnic. As the time for this activity approaches, Zümrüt is concerned that they will not be able to find space in the front area of the park on the seaside. The narrator explains in detail how much change this park has made in Kozlukite women’s lives who enjoy having picnics there in the daytime with their daughters (209). In the evenings, they go there together with their husbands. In Istanbul, where public green space is scarce, some city inhabitants even use the little green patches next to roads for picnicking when the parks are all full. Picnics in ‘inappropriate places’ disgust elitists who regard it as an act in conflict with urban manners. Instead of criticising the lack of access to green spaces in the city they attack these picnickers, claiming that they are unaware of urban civilities. In the novel, Meryem illustrates the need for green space as an issue of the right to access to recreational areas by showing it through the characters’ viewpoint.

zh: 小说几乎完全以科兹卢克为场景，其中最重要的例外是“比宫殿还大的人”一章（202—208），讲述贾维特与一位阅历丰富、名叫希贾比的渔夫的友谊，后者最终自杀。这段友谊的片段，通过倒叙进入小说，置于贾维特从希贾比那里继承的蓝色皮卡的故事框架之中。
en: The novel is almost entirely set in Kozluk and the most important exception to this is the chapter entitled “The Man Who Is Larger than Palaces” (202–208), which is about Cavit’s friendship with a sophisticated fisherman called Hicabi, who eventually commits suicide. Moments from this friendship enter the novel via flashback within the frame of the story of Cavit’s blue pickup, which he inherited from Hicabi.

zh: 贾维特与希贾比初次见面是在耶尼卡帕的一家咖啡馆。他们立刻成为朋友，沿着海岸从耶尼卡帕走到恰特拉德卡帕。在那里，希贾比指着托普卡帕宫，问贾维特是否见过宫殿。随后，他邀请贾维特进入一座想象的宫殿，两人都假装身在托普卡帕宫。这个小游戏之后，他们继续散步，希贾比向贾维特讲述博斯普鲁斯海峡和渔船的故事。希贾比怀念旧伊斯坦布尔。贾维特引述他谈论这座城市的话：“那时候伊斯坦布尔才叫伊斯坦布尔”（204）；“

children: 把那时候整个伊斯坦布尔凑在一起，一个小贩就能把它背走

zh: ”（205）。希贾比凭借旺盛的想象力编出关于那些日子的故事。随着友谊加深，贾维特得知希贾比过去热衷阅读，还参加过剧团。这让从未进过剧院的贾维特很惊讶。两人开着希贾比的蓝色皮卡，走遍伊斯坦布尔：“靠着这辆皮卡，他们一天去埃于普，在埋葬于那里的圣人墓前祈祷，一天又在萨勒耶尔同渔民举瓶喝葡萄酒。他们要么在希莱偏远岩石上方的弯道上急转，要么在恰塔尔贾一带村庄的咖啡馆里同农民聊天”（206）。因为与希贾比的友谊，贾维特体验到伊斯坦布尔不同的一面。换言之，在与希贾比相处的时间里，他通过城市景观与历史，对城市形成了某种依恋。
en: Cavit first meets Hicabi at a coffee house in Yenikapı. They instantly become friends and have a walk on the shore from Yenikapı to Çatladıkapı. Here, Hicabi points out Topkapı Palace and asks Cavit if he has ever seen a palace. Then he invites him into an imaginary palace and they both pretend to be in Topkapı Palace. After that little game, as they continue their walk, Hicabi tells Cavit stories about the Bosporus, as well as about fishing boats. Hicabi is nostalgic about old Istanbul. Cavit cites his words on the city: “those were the times when Istanbul was Istanbul” (204); “

” (205). Hicabi invents stories about those days with a powerful imagination. As their friendship deepens, Cavit learns that in the past Hicabi was an avid reader, and engaged in a theatre group. This surprises Cavit who has never been to a theatre. The pair drive around Istanbul in Hicabi’s blue pickup: “One day they were going to Eyüp and praying before the holy men buried there, one day they were tossing back their wine bottles with the fishermen in Sarıyer, thanks to this pickup. They were either swerving round the bends over the remote rocks of Şile, or chatting with peasants in the coffeehouses of villages around Çatalca” (206). Owing to his friendship with Hicabi, Cavit experiences a different face of Istanbul. In other words, he develops a certain attachment to the city, through its sights and history, during the time he spends with Hicabi.

zh: 希贾比虽是次要人物，却对小说关于城市身份的表达至关重要。他是小说中唯一对城市怀有依恋的人。这个深深依恋城市的人怀念旧日时光，是重要细节。梅里耶姆以独特方式，通过希贾比这样一个普通民众人物，展开对过去伊斯坦布尔的怀旧主题。如前面多次讨论的，关于伊斯坦布尔的怀旧话语在精英中广泛流行，并把矛头指向城市中的迁入者。通过希贾比这一人物，梅里耶姆强调，人们可以怀念伊斯坦布尔消失的美，而不把这种损失归咎于迁入者；希贾比正是这样做的。通过引入这个人物，梅里耶姆挑战了伊斯坦布尔人与“非伊斯坦布尔人”二分法的两大基本陈词滥调。第一，为城市的负面变化感到悲伤的，并不只有精英。第二，并非出生于此的居民，也能通过欣赏城市之美与遗产、并感到有责任帮助保护它们，而对城市产生深厚依恋。
en: Hicabi is a minor yet crucial character regarding the novel’s messages about urban identity. In the novel, he is the only character who has an attachment to the city. It is an important detail that this person strongly attached to the city is nostalgic about its former days. Meryem, in a unique manner, develops the theme of nostalgia for a past Istanbul through a character like Hicabi, who is a man of the people. As discussed various times previously, nostalgic discourse about Istanbul is widespread among the elite and targets the migrants in the city. Through the character of Hicabi, Meryem stresses that it is possible to long for the disappeared beauties of Istanbul without blaming migrants for the loss, which is what Hicabi does. Introducing this character, Meryem challenges the dichotomy between Istanbulites and ‘non-Istanbulites’ over its two fundamental clichés. First, it is not only the elite who are sad about the negative changes in the city. Second, inhabitants who were not born in the city can develop a strong attachment to it by appreciating its beauty and heritage and feeling a responsibility to help preserve it.

zh: 结论

《人各有别》前面的篇页中，叙述者评论道，迁入者起初在城市中感到不安，后来却“能够向伊斯坦布尔发起挑战”（32）。这样的措辞，乍看可能略微偏向反迁入者话语：迁入者到来，过了一阵便开始提出要求。然而，通观全书便会发现，这一说法指的是迁入者如何在城市中挣扎，争取自己的权利。梅里耶姆提醒人们关注乡村迁入者在城市中面临的艰难。她塑造小说人物时，强调他们在城市环境中生存下去的意志，而非呼唤怜悯。小说结尾在这方面尤其有力。
en: In the earlier pages of

, the narrator comments that after feeling insecure in the city at the beginning, migrants “were able to challenge Istanbul” (32). Such a wording might first sound slightly on the side of the anti-migrant discourse: migrants arrive and after a while they become demanding. However, when we consider the book in its entirety, it becomes clear that this phrasing is a reference to the way migrants struggle and fight for their rights in the city. Meryem draws attention to the hardship rural migrants face in the city. She creates the characters in her novel with emphasis on their will to survive in the urban setting rather than a call for pity. The ending of the book is particularly powerful in this respect.

zh: 末章题为“生活像博斯普鲁斯海峡的水一样流淌”（284），时值宗教节日，科兹卢克人穿上最好的衣服，去拜访亲友邻里。

祖姆鲁特、贾维特和孩子们坐在蓝色皮卡里，行驶在拜访的路上。在小说最后的场景中，皮卡开到了博斯普鲁斯大桥中央。贾维特驾车过桥，陷入沉思：“贾维特很满足。有那么一刻，他瞥了一眼那些在阳光下各自闪耀如珠宝的宅邸、宫殿，又望了望伊斯坦布尔城平静的海峡水面；这座城市铺展在两块巨大大陆的两岸”（285）。他想起自己听说，即便看上去平静，博斯普鲁斯海峡水面之下也总有强劲的水流；在他看来，这如同生活的流动：“生活不也像流过海峡的水一样奔流吗？”
en: In the final chapter, entitled “Life Flows like the Water of the Bosporus” (284), it is the time of a religious holiday and Kozlukites are in their best outfits to visit their relatives and neighbours.

Zümrüt, Cavit and their children are in the blue pickup on their way to their visits. In the final scene of the novel, the pickup is in the middle of the Bosporus Bridge. Cavit dives into his thoughts as he drives over the bridge: “Cavit was content. At one point, he took a glance at the mansions, each glittering like a piece of jewellery in the sun, the palaces and again the still waters of the straits of the city of Istanbul, which expanded on the two sides of the two gigantic continents” (285). He remembers hearing that even when it seems calm there is always a strong current under the Bosporus and this resembles the flow of life to him: “was not life running like the waters running through the straits?”

zh: 通过自由间接话语和心理叙述呈现贾维特的思想与感受之后，轮到叙述者分享自己的想法。她解释，贾维特和祖姆鲁特这样的人，如何在宗教节日拜访亲人，恭敬有礼，“让廉价的薄荷糖或可可味糖果在口中融化”（286）。她补充：“他们在表明，自己能够顶住那股潮流，顶住所有这些苦难，此外还有种种烦恼和忧虑［……］，与其说生活压倒了他们，不如说他们压倒了生活，嗯，他们有点儿像在彼此较劲”（286）。这段解释之后，是全书的最后一句：“贾维特踩下油门”（286）。
en: After presenting Cavit’s thoughts and feelings through free indirect discourse and psycho-narration, it is the narrator’s turn to share her thoughts. She explains how people like Cavit and Zümrüt visit family members on religious holidays and behave respectfully “melt[ing] cheap mint or cacao-flavoured sweets on their palates” (286). She adds that: “they were exhibiting that they could stand up against that tide, all that distress, aside from all that nuisance and worry [...] rather than life prevailing over them, they were prevailing over life, well, they were sort of defying each other a little bit” (286). After this explanation comes the final sentence of the book: “Cavit stepped on the gas” (286).

zh: 叙述者描写贾维特在博斯普鲁斯大桥上沉思时，使用了奥斯曼语短语“şehr-i İstanbul”（伊斯坦布尔城）（285）。这一措辞似乎暗示贾维特那一刻的愉悦：他正在一座曾作为奥斯曼帝国首都近五百年的历史城市中，欣赏令人惊叹的景色。小说的两大核心意旨在结尾交织：科兹卢克人与城市的隔绝，以及他们为在其中生存而面对的艰难。在城市中、在与外界隔绝的科兹卢克旧棚户区里经历种种挣扎之后，他们也有时能够享受伊斯坦布尔的景观与历史遗产，至少在宗教节日这样的特殊时刻可以如此。这里的大桥仿佛是城市中心与边缘之间联系的隐喻：中心地区、历史建筑、宫殿和宅邸，以及城市郊外的旧棚户区，共同组成伊斯坦布尔。因此，无论住在哪里，城市都属于它的所有居民。
en: As the narrator describes Cavit’s contemplation on the Bosporus Bridge she uses the Ottoman phrase of “şehr-i İstanbul” (the city of Istanbul) (285). This word choice seems to imply Cavit’s pleasure at that moment: he is enjoying an amazing view in a historical city which served as the capital of the Ottoman Empire for almost five centuries. The two central tenets of the novel intertwine in its ending: Kozlukites’ isolation from the city and the hardships they face to survive in it. After all their struggle in the city, in the isolated former shanty town of Kozluk, there are times they can enjoy Istanbul with its views and historical heritage, at least on a special occasion like a religious holiday. The bridge here sounds like a metaphor for the connection between the centre and the periphery of the city: central areas, historic buildings, palaces and mansions, as well as former shanty towns on the outskirts of the city, they all together constitute Istanbul. Consequently, the city belongs to all of its inhabitants wherever they live.

zh: 《人各有别》中有几处幽默，听来可能略微倾向反迁入者话语和／或精英主义话语。如前所述，关于科兹卢克孩子不愿读书、年轻人倾向犯罪的段落，就是主要例子。叙述者描写科兹卢克新娘发型时选用“
”（漫画化）一词，也带有类似语调（11）。然而，考虑小说的总体立场，这种幽默似乎出于
的意图，而不是
。书写生活在城市偏远角落的迁入者时，梅里耶姆现实而客观，同时怀有同情，呼唤共情而非怜悯。
en: Throughout

, there are a couple of instances when the humour might sound slightly as if it is leaning towards an anti-migrant and/or elitist discourse. As mentioned earlier, the passages about Kozlukite children’s disinclination to study and the youngsters’ tendency towards crime are the main examples of this. The narrator’s word choice of “

” (caricatured) while describing the hair style of Kozlukite brides has a similar tone (11). However, given the overall position of the novel, this humour appears to stem from the intention of laughing
Kozlukites rather than laughing
them. Addressing the life of migrants in remote corners of the city, Meryem is realistic and objective, yet sympathetic, and calls for empathy rather than pity.

zh: 科兹卢克体现了那些在公众观念中遭到鄙视、被污名化为
的街区。梅里耶姆小说导言的最后一段，几乎诗意地描绘了那些不断被贬为
之流的城市居民的生活：“等到科兹卢克的父母们也抱上盼望已久的孙辈，他们便开始谈论来世，就像在谈论隔壁那条街”（12）。她又说：“当他们在沉重的羊毛被下，或在公立医院昏暗的走廊里悄然死去，没有人会察觉。这个故事属于他们”（12）。
en: Kozluk is an illustration of neighbourhoods looked down on and stigmatised as
in public opinion. The final passage of Meryem’s introduction to her novel comes to the fore almost as a poetic depiction of the lives of those city inhabitants constantly humiliated as

types: “once Kozlukite mothers and fathers also have the grandchildren whom they were looking forward to, they start talking about the next world like they are talking about the next street” (12). She adds: “when they silently die under their heavy wool duvets or in the dim corridors of state hospitals, no one will be any the wiser. This story is theirs” (12).

zh: 《人各有别》中，梅里耶姆既不理想化科兹卢克，也不把当地人塑造成英雄或天使。她只是以共情接近他们，同时不牺牲对这个孤立旧棚户区生活负面方面、居民平庸之处，以及流氓无产阶级堕落行径的现实主义观察。她处理这些问题时不妄下道德判断，并通过巧妙运用幽默保持共情视角。她指出所谓
居民经历的种种匮乏，从基本市政服务，到休闲与社会交往的需要，从而明智地处理城市权利主题。因此，她邀请读者摆脱偏见，从另一角度看待那些外观杂乱无章、被贬斥为
的旧棚户区，以及其中贫穷且大多缺乏教育的人们。
en: In

, Meryem does not idealise Kozluk nor portray its people as heroes or angels. She simply approaches them with empathy, without sacrificing a realistic perspective about the negative aspects of life in this isolated former shanty town, the banal sides of its people, and the degenerate ways of the lumpen proletariat. She addresses these issues without being judgemental, while maintaining an empathetic perspective with the skilful implementation of humour. She intelligently treats the themes of the right to the city by pointing out all sorts of deprivation the people of the so-called
experience: from basic municipal services to the needs regarding recreation and socialisation. Consequently, she invites her readers to view the amorphous looking former shanty towns dismissed as
and their poor, mostly uneducated people from a different angle free of prejudice.

zh: 《在边缘》与《人各有别》：比较分析
en: On the Periphery and It Takes All Kinds: A Comparative Analysis

zh: 《在边缘》没有通常意义上的情节：盖奇金关注的是精神状态，而非事件。主人公的视角主导全书。他是一名男子，可能是知识分子，出身于乡村迁入家庭。他性格内向，与家人亲戚来往不密切。他在城市中感到异化，认为这里混乱而压抑。他的异化并不源于迁入家庭背景。他属于中心，也同样属于边缘；或者更准确地说，他对中心缺乏归属，对边缘也一样。作品让读者通过他的视角，看见一个令人感到幽闭的城市。叙述者始终保持距离，制造出一种感觉：仿佛这位冷淡、客观的主人公，以第三人称讲述自己的经验，由此让人接近真实的城市。这种叙述既没有局外人的共情，也没有明显的偏见。
en: does not have a plot in the usual sense of the word: Geçgin focuses on states of mind rather than events. The perspective of the protagonist dominates the novel. This is a man, probably an intellectual, who comes from a rural migrant family. He is an introvert who does not keep close contact with his family and relatives. He feels alienated in the city, which he perceives as a chaotic and depressing place. The reason for his alienation does not stem from his migrant family background. He belongs to the centre as much as he belongs to the periphery; or rather, he lacks a belonging to the centre as much as he does to the periphery. The work enables readers to see the city from his perspective as a claustrophobic place. The narrator is detached throughout the book, creating a feeling as if the protagonist, who is an aloof and objective person, is speaking about his own experiences in the third person and thus giving access to the actual city. There is neither an outsider’s empathy, nor obvious prejudice in this narration.

zh: 《人各有别》有界定清晰的情节，包含中心事件与核心事件，通过倒叙和离题插叙，以非线性结构展开。梅里耶姆引入所有主要人物的视角，叙述者也始终有鲜明的存在感。全书以祖姆鲁特和埃尔马斯姐妹的视角为中心，打开了一扇通过女性眼光观察边缘生活的门。
en: has a well-defined plot with central and kernel events, developed in a non-linear structure with flashbacks and digressions. Meryem introduces the perspectives of all the major characters, and the narrator also has a distinct presence throughout the novel. With the perspectives of sisters Zümrüt and Elmas at its centre, the book opens a gateway to life on the periphery through the eyes of women.

zh: 比较两部作品人物的阶级位置，或许能说明这两种边缘形态中的隔绝与排斥机制。盖奇金在小说中并不把边缘等同于隔绝。因吉尔柯伊及同一铁路沿线的其他工人阶级街区，似乎彼此连接，也与城市相连，因为居民是劳动力队伍的积极组成部分：他们为城市生产。《人各有别》中的科兹卢克这样的地方，劳动潜力却是多余的，这导致街区及居民的隔绝。城市大体上不需要科兹卢克和它的居民，因此他们无法与城市相连，因为他们在其中没有角色。男人在附近找零工，女人到邻近封闭式社区的人家做钟点清洁工，仅此而已。
en: A comparison of the class positions of the characters in the two works might clarify the mechanisms of isolation and exclusion in these two versions of periphery. In his novel, Geçgin does not equate periphery with isolation. İncirköy and various other working-class neighbourhoods on the same railway route seem to be connected with each other and with the city, since their inhabitants are an active part of the labour force: they produce for the city. In

, in a place such as Kozluk, the labour potential is redundant and this results in the isolation of the neighbourhood and its inhabitants. For the most part, the city does not need Kozluk and its dwellers, therefore they cannot connect with it, since they have no role in it. The men find odd jobs in the vicinity, the women go to houses in the gated communities nearby as daily cleaners, and that is all.

zh: 《在边缘》中因吉尔柯伊的原型卡兹勒切什梅，距离塔克西姆或贝希克塔什等城市中心地区约十公里，而《人各有别》暗示科兹卢克要遥远得多。科兹卢克似乎再现了距塔克西姆约四十公里的哈德姆柯伊附近的街区，用“边缘的边缘”来形容最为贴切。
en: Kazlıçeşme, the model for İncirköy in
, is around ten kilometres from the central areas of the city, such as Taksim or Beşiktaş, while Kozluk in

is implied to be much more remote. Kozluk seems to be a representation of neighbourhoods near Hadımköy, which is about forty kilometres from Taksim, and can best be described as the periphery of the periphery.

zh: 《在边缘》的因吉尔柯伊靠近巴克尔库莱，后者以巴克尔柯伊这一重要的社会文化生活中心为原型；而《人各有别》中，没有这样一个可供科兹卢克人参与的城市中心。《在边缘》多次提及因吉尔柯伊原型卡兹勒切什梅的拜占庭与希腊历史。丰富的历史和世界主义遗产，使这里成为有自身身份的地方。科兹卢克的原型则是除了居民之外无人知晓的旧棚户区，它没有一段可以将自身与城市历史相连的历史。
en: İncirköy in
is close to Bakırkule, inspired by Bakırköy, an important centre of social and cultural life; while in
there is no such urban centre Kozlukites can be a part of. In

, there are various references to the Byzantine and Greek past of Kazlıçeşme, the model for İncirköy. With a rich history and the legacy of a cosmopolitan heritage, this is a place with an identity. Kozluk, inspired by former shanty towns nobody except for their dwellers know about, does not have a history that can connect it with the history of the city.

zh: 盖奇金与梅里耶姆处理城市身份主题的方式不同。《在边缘》中，盖奇金主要将迁入者描写为工人阶级成员；梅里耶姆小说中的迁入者，则属于不稳定无产者或流氓无产阶级。虽然因吉尔柯伊和科兹卢克都再现了伊斯坦布尔那些在20世纪80年代以公寓楼取代棚屋的旧棚户区，但作为街区，它们的社会构成差异很大。《在边缘》的主要场景之一因吉尔柯伊，是老工人阶级街区，居民多为曾在塔什勒巴工厂工作的工人。那些工厂后来迁出此地，却没有改变因吉尔柯伊作为工人阶级街区的身份。换言之，因吉尔柯伊大多数人口是凭正规部门稳定的工人工作，成功在伊斯坦布尔建立生活的迁入者。另一方面，《人各有别》的场景科兹卢克，其居民则是只能找到不稳定工作的穷人。小说某处告诉我们，整个科兹卢克只有一个女人有“有文件的”（
）工作（Meryem 2008，245），意思是雇主为她缴纳社会保险。科兹卢克男人通常失业，即使有工作也大多是临时的。简言之，因吉尔柯伊是无产阶级街区，而科兹卢克的共同体则由不稳定无产者与流氓无产阶级共同构成。因此，因吉尔柯伊居民的常态是努力工作，伊斯这样的闲荡者偏离了这一常态；科兹卢克的常态则是临时工作或失业，闲荡者几乎成了标准形态。
en: Geçgin and Meryem differ in how they treat the theme of urban identity. In

, Geçgin depicts migrants mostly as members of the working class, while the migrants in Meryem’s novel belong to either the precariat or the lumpen proletariat. While both İncirköy and Kozluk represent former shanty towns of Istanbul, where shanties were replaced with apartment buildings in the 1980s, they bear considerable differences between their fabrics as neighbourhoods. İncirköy, one of the primary locations of the setting in

, is an old working-class neighbourhood mostly inhabited by workers who have been employed in the factories of Taşlıbağ. Eventually, these factories get removed from this area, but this does not change the identity of İncirköy as a working-class neighbourhood. In other words, the majority of İncirköy’s population comprises migrants who have managed to establish a life in Istanbul with steady jobs as workers in the formal sector. In Kozluk, the setting of
, on the other hand, inhabitants are poor people who can only find precarious work. At one point in the novel, we learn that there is only one woman in Kozluk who has a “documented” (

) (Meryem 2008, 245) job, which means her employer pays her social security taxes. Kozluk’s men are usually unemployed and when they have jobs these are mostly temporary. In brief, İncirköy is a neighbourhood of the proletariat, while Kozluk’s community is a combination of the precariat and the lumpen proletariat. Consequently, the norm for the inhabitants of İncirköy is working hard, and idlers, like İs, are a deviation from this norm; while the norm for Kozluk is either temporary work or unemployment, thus idlers are almost standard.

zh: 两处街区共同体面貌的差异，对犯罪问题具有根本意义。在两部小说中，闲荡者似乎都有犯罪倾向，主要是小偷小摸。《在边缘》中，盖奇金通过伊斯的故事简略处理这一主题。他没有披露伊斯犯罪的细节，但我们可以推知，伊斯从未加入街区内外的任何团伙。他的犯罪似乎与居住地无关，而是出于自身不循常规的偏离。然而，在《人各有别》中，犯罪在故事里占据重要位置，因为主要人物之一乔什昆刚刚出狱。他最亲近的朋友也涉及轻微犯罪，这一细节暗示科兹卢克青年有结成类似帮派群体的倾向。简言之，两部作品对阻止或导致失范的条件，都持现实主义态度。在《在边缘》中，盖奇金现实地将棚户区描绘为没有失范的地方；在《人各有别》中，梅里耶姆则指出，当向上流动的希望和世界主义的团结缺失时，旧棚户区存在失范的可能。
en: This difference between the profiles of the two neighbourhood communities is of fundamental significance as regards the issue of crime. In both novels, idlers seem to have a tendency to crime, mainly petty crime. In

, Geçgin addresses this theme briefly in the story of İs. He does not disclose the details of İs’s crime, but we can infer that he was never part of a gang, either inside or outside of the neighbourhood. His crime does not seem to have any connection with the place he lives in, it is rather a deviation stemming from his eccentricity. However, in

, crime has an important presence in the story, since Coşkun, one of the major characters, has recently been released from prison. His closest friends are also involved in petty crime, a detail that implies a tendency amongst the youngsters of Kozluk to form gang-like groups. In brief, both works are realistic about the conditions that prevent, or lead to, anomie. In
, Geçgin portrays shanty towns realistically as places where anomie did not exist, while in
Meryem points out the potential for anomie in former shanty towns in the absence of hope of upward mobility and cosmopolitan solidarity.

zh: 《在边缘》中，盖奇金呈现了多个父子故事，把家庭纽带和亲属关系描写为伊斯坦布尔迁入者的核心团结网络。然而，主人公过的是个体的生活，非常符合城市环境。书中没有他与亡父发生冲突或决裂的故事；他只是一个孤独的城市人。《人各有别》中，取代父子冲突的，是年长与年幼手足之间的紧张关系：祖姆鲁特与埃尔马斯、贾维特与乔什昆。最后，埃尔马斯和乔什昆一起逃走了；但这是否意味着个体化的行动，仍相当含混。
en: In

, Geçgin presents various father and son stories, and depicts family ties and kinship relations as the central solidarity network of migrants in Istanbul. The protagonist of the novel, however, has the life of an individual, very much in line with the urban setting. No story of conflict or separation between him and his late father appears, he is simply a solitary urbanite. In

, instead of the father and son conflict, we have the tension between older and younger siblings: Zümrüt vs Elmas; Cavit vs Coşkun. In the end, Elmas and Coşkun run away together; but it is rather vague if this is an act of individualisation.

zh: 在《在边缘》中，盖奇金在一定程度上忽略了迁移的性别维度：他只是暗示，从乡村转到城市环境，女性生活并未发生多大变化。《人各有别》中，梅里耶姆描写了女性对消费主义的痴迷；在她们自己看来，这是获得城市身份的唯一方式。
en: In
, Geçgin somewhat ignores the gender aspect of migration: he simply hints that women’s lives do not change much with the shift from the rural to the urban context. In
, Meryem depicts women’s obsession with consumerism as the only way, to their mind, of adopting an urban identity.

zh: 尽管存在上述种种差异，两部作品场景中的生活，就未得到落实的城市权利而言，仍有显著相似性。在两部作品中，市政服务的获取受限，都作为重要主题浮现出来。与之相关，《人各有别》中的停水、停电和污染问题成为母题。盖奇金在《在边缘》中也运用污水问题、老鼠等类似母题，既展开这一主题，又强化压抑的氛围。简言之，《人各有别》以契合其幽默讽刺语调的方式容纳这一主题，并强调迁入者的求生斗争；而在《在边缘》中，这些细节则成为小说阴暗意象的核心要素。
en: Despite all their differences discussed so far, the similarities of life in the settings of the two works as regards the unimplemented right to the city are significant. In both of them, limited access to municipal services comes to the fore as an important theme. Related to that, water and electricity cuts, as well as pollution problems, appear as motifs in
. Geçgin uses similar motifs in
, such as sewage problems and rats, to develop this theme as well as to reinforce a depressing atmosphere. In short,
contains this theme in line with its humorous, sarcastic tone and with an accent on migrants’ struggle for survival; while in
such details appear as central elements of the novel’s dark imagery.

zh: 享有公园等城市休闲空间的权利，是两位作者在小说中以相似方式处理的城市权利主题的另一面。能否利用公共空间，尤其是绿地，是两部作品的重要主题。《在边缘》中，公园在主人公的日常生活里处于中心位置。《人各有别》中，梅里耶姆既通过野餐事件，也通过将科兹卢克中心这一购物中心设定为街区居民、尤其年轻人闲暇活动的场所，强调对公园和类似区域的需要。两部作品中，缺少社区中心——城市居民，特别是年轻人，可以不用花钱便与同龄人见面、交往，通过爱好从事有创造性的活动，或者学习新技能的地方——成为城市权利未获充分承认的另一维度。因此，闲散在两部小说中都成为重要母题，也与劳动权主题相连。
en: The right to access to urban recreational spaces, such as parks, is another aspect of the right to the city theme which the two authors treat similarly in their novels. The opportunity, or the absence thereof, to benefit from public space, particularly green areas, is a major theme in both works. In
, parks have a central place in the protagonist’s daily life. In

, Meryem underscores the need for parks and similar areas, both through the incident of the picnic and by locating the Kozluk Center, a shopping mall, as the locus of free time activity in the neighbourhood, especially for youngsters. In both works, the lack of community centres where city inhabitants, especially the young, can meet and socialise with their peers without spending money, where they can be productive with hobbies or acquire new skills, comes to the fore as another dimension of the limited recognition of the right to the city. Thus, idleness appears as an important motif in both novels, also connected with the theme of the right to work.

zh: 还有一点或许值得补充：两部作品都以20世纪80年代末以后为背景，因此与伊斯坦布尔新自由主义化和全球化相关的多种母题，不可避免地进入作品。全球化城市中的经济租金创造，就是两部作品共有的主题之一：《在边缘》中，皮革工业迁出卡兹勒切什梅暗示了这一点；《人各有别》则更直接，祖姆鲁特解释，科兹卢克中心建成后，科兹卢克的公寓更值钱了（Meryem 2008，104）。在后者中，封闭式社区作为与经济租金创造和城市碎片化均相关的母题出现。在《在边缘》中，盖奇金描写主人公行走时看到的蒂内尔街区加拉塔周边的变化，简略触及绅士化（Geçgin 2003，160）。他还在小说中引入外国移民和大量游客，作为与城市全球化有关的母题。城市贫困作为新自由主义城市经济与社会弊病的另一面，也在两书中可见。在《在边缘》中，它通过贯穿全书的卖纸巾的孩子、吸胶者、乞丐和无家可归者的存在进入作品；在《人各有别》中，则从科兹卢克人的总体生活水准中清楚显现。
en: It might also be useful to add that various motifs related to the neoliberalisation and globalisation of Istanbul enter the two works, inevitably, since they are both set after the end of the 1980s. The economic rent creation in the globalising city is one such theme appearing in both of them: in
, the removal of the leather industry from Kazlıçeşme implies it, while in

, in a rather direct expression, Zümrüt explains that after the Kozluk Center was built, the apartments of Kozluk became more valuable (Meryem 2008, 104). In this novel, gated communities appear as a motif related to both economic rent creation and urban fragmentation. In

, Geçgin briefly addresses gentrification by describing the changes around Galata in the Tünel neighbourhood, as the protagonist walks around the area (Geçgin 2003, 160). Geçgin also introduces foreign migrants and a large number of tourists as motifs, in his novel, related to the globalisation of the city. Urban poverty, another aspect of the neoliberal city’s economic and social ills, is also visible in both books. This enters
via the presence of children selling tissue paper, glue-sniffers, beggars and the homeless throughout the story. In
it becomes clear in the Kozlukites’ overall standard of living.

zh: 两部小说都在城市中心而非边缘结束，这是有趣的相似点。而且在两个结尾中，人物都凝望着伊斯坦布尔最鲜明的象征——博斯普鲁斯海峡——思索人生。《在边缘》中，主人公长途步行后抵达贝希克塔什，就在准备回家时改变主意，留了下来。他开始凝望码头、大海和周围的人。叙述者详细描述他看见什么，而非想些什么，邀请读者在海浪拍岸时同他一起欣赏景色，强调城市居民凝望同一景色、沉思人生时彼此之间的联系。《人各有别》结尾，祖姆鲁特、丈夫与儿子们乘着皮卡，在宗教节日期间去拜访亲戚。车子驶过博斯普鲁斯大桥时，贾维特被海峡水流的样子迷住，乐观地思索生活，想着尽管困难重重，自己和家人依然站立着。这部几乎完全以科兹卢克为场景、强调它同伊斯坦布尔中心脱节的小说，却结束在城市正中心，结束在连接两块大陆、强有力地象征融入的博斯普鲁斯大桥上。收束全书时，梅里耶姆将人物从科兹卢克带到博斯普鲁斯大桥，似乎暗示中心与边缘之间的联系。虽然两部作品展开中心与边缘主题的方式很不相同，其结尾却传达了相似的信息：边缘的人们属于伊斯坦布尔，伊斯坦布尔也属于他们，正如它属于中心的居民一样。
en: Both novels end in the centre of the city rather than on the periphery, which is an interesting similarity. Furthermore, in both endings, the characters contemplate life as they watch the Bosporus, the ultimate symbol of Istanbul. In

, the protagonist arrives at Beşiktaş after a long walk and just as he is about to go back home, he changes his mind and stays. He starts gazing at the pier, the sea and the people around. The narrator explains in detail what he sees, rather than what he thinks, inviting the reader to enjoy this view with him as the waves hit the shore, emphasising a connection between the inhabitants of the city as they gaze at the same view and contemplate life. At the conclusion of

, Zümrüt, her husband and their sons are in their pickup on their way to visit relatives for a religious holiday. As they are driving over the Bosporus Bridge, Cavit, mesmerised by the way the water runs in the Bosporus, contemplates life with optimism, thinking that despite all the difficulties, he and his family are still standing. The novel, which is almost entirely set in Kozluk, with emphasis on its disconnectedness with the centre of Istanbul, ends at the very centre of the city, on the Bosporus Bridge which links two continents, a powerful symbol of integration. As she brings her book to a close, Meryem seems to imply a connection between the centre and the periphery, bringing her characters from Kozluk to the Bosporus Bridge. Although in the two works the theme of centre and periphery are developed in quite dissimilar ways, in their endings they convey a similar message: the people of the periphery belong to Istanbul and Istanbul belongs to them as much as it does to the inhabitants of the centre.
